verses.1:1: And it happened after Alexander, son of Philip, the Macedonian, who came out from the land of Kittim, had struck down Darius, king of the Persians and Medes, that he reigned in his place, first over Greece.
verses.1:2: And he waged many wars, seized strongholds, and slaughtered kings,
verses.1:3: and he passed through to the ends of the earth and took plunder from a multitude of nations. And the earth became quiet before him, and he was exalted, and his heart was lifted up.
verses.1:4: And he gathered an exceedingly strong army, and ruled over countries, nations, and dominions, and they became tributary to him.
verses.1:5: And after these things he fell onto his bed, and he knew that he was dying.
verses.1:6: And he called his honored servants who had been brought up with him from youth, and he divided his kingdom among them while he was still alive.
verses.1:7: And Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
verses.1:8: And his servants took control, each in his own place;
verses.1:9: and they all put on diadems after he died, and their sons after them for many years; and they multiplied evils on the earth.
verses.1:10: And there came out from them a sinful root, Antiochus Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king, who had been a hostage in Rome. And he began to reign in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
verses.1:11: In those days there came out from Israel a lawless son, and they persuaded many, saying, "Let us go and make a covenant with the nations around us, for from the time we were separated by them, many evils have found us."
verses.1:12: And the word seemed good in their eyes.
verses.1:13: And some of the people were eager and went to the king; and they gave them authority to observe the ordinances of the nations.
verses.1:14: And they built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the nations.
verses.1:15: And they made foreskins for themselves, and turned away from the holy covenant; and they yoked themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.
verses.1:16: And the kingdom was established before Antiochus, and he intended to reign over the land of Egypt, so that he might reign over the two kingdoms.
verses.1:17: And he entered Egypt with a heavy force, with chariots and elephants, and with horsemen and a great fleet.
verses.1:18: And he waged war against Ptolemy, the king of Egypt; and Ptolemy turned back from before him and fled, and many fell wounded.
verses.1:19: And they captured the fortified cities in the land of Egypt, and he took the plunder of the land of Egypt.
verses.1:20: And Antiochus returned after striking down Egypt in the one hundred and forty-third year, and he went up against Israel and Jerusalem with a heavy force.
verses.1:21: And he entered the sanctuary in arrogance, and he took the golden altar, the lampstand for the light and all its utensils,
verses.1:22: and the table of the presentation, the libation cups, the bowls, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, and the golden ornamentation on the front of the temple; and he stripped off everything.
verses.1:23: And he took the silver and the gold, and the precious vessels; and he took the hidden treasures that he found.
verses.1:24: And having taken everything, he departed to his own land. And they committed slaughter, and spoke with great arrogance.
verses.1:25: And there was great mourning upon Israel in every place of theirs.
verses.1:26: And rulers and elders groaned, virgins and young men grew weak, and the beauty of the women was altered.
verses.1:27: Every bridegroom took up a lament; she who sat in the bridal chamber was in mourning.
verses.1:28: And the land was shaken for those who lived in it, and the whole house of Jacob clothed itself with shame.
verses.1:29: After two full years, the king sent a chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a heavy force.
verses.1:30: And he spoke peaceful words to them in deceit, and they trusted him, and he fell upon the city suddenly, and struck it with a great blow, and destroyed many people from Israel.
verses.1:31: And he took the plunder of the city and burned it with fire, and tore down its houses and its walls all around,
verses.1:32: and he took the women and the children captive, and they took possession of the livestock.
verses.1:33: And they built up the city of David with a great and strong wall, with strong towers, and it became a citadel for them.
verses.1:34: And they placed there a sinful nation, lawless men, and they grew strong in it.
verses.1:35: And they stored up weapons and food, and having gathered the plunder of Jerusalem, they deposited it there; and it became a great snare,
verses.1:36: and it became an ambush against the sanctuary and an evil adversary to Israel continually.
verses.1:37: And they shed innocent blood all around the sanctuary, and they polluted the sanctuary.
verses.1:38: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them, and she became a dwelling place of strangers; and she became a stranger to her offspring, and her children were forsaking her.
verses.1:39: Her sanctuary was made desolate like a wilderness; her festivals were turned into mourning, her Sabbaths into reproach, her honor into contempt.
verses.1:40: According to her glory, her dishonor was multiplied, and her exaltation was turned into mourning.
verses.1:41: And the king wrote to his whole kingdom that all should be one people,
verses.1:42: and that each one should forsake his own customs; and all the nations agreed according to the word of the king.
verses.1:43: And many from Israel were pleased with his worship, and sacrificed to the idols, and profaned the Sabbath.
verses.1:44: And the king sent letters by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, to go after customs foreign to the land,
verses.1:45: and to forbid burnt offerings and sacrifices and a drink offering from the sanctuary, and to profane Sabbaths and festivals,
verses.1:46: and to defile the sanctuary and holy ones;
verses.1:47: to build altars and sacred precincts and idols, and to sacrifice swine and unclean animals,
verses.1:48: and to leave their sons uncircumcised, to make their souls abominable with every impure thing and to profane them,
verses.1:49: so as to forget the law and change all the ordinances.
verses.1:50: And whoever does not act according to the word of the king will die.
verses.1:51: According to all these words he wrote to his kingdom, and he appointed overseers over all the people; and he commanded the cities of Judah to offer sacrifices city by city.
verses.1:52: And many from the people gathered together to them, everyone who forsook the law; and they committed evils in the land,
verses.1:53: and they forced Israel into hiding places, in every place of refuge of theirs.
verses.1:54: And on the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the forty-fifth year, they built an abomination of desolation upon the altar; and in the cities of Judah all around they built altars,
verses.1:55: and at the windows of the houses and in the streets they burned incense.
verses.1:56: And the books of the law that they found, they tore to pieces and burned with fire.
verses.1:57: And wherever a book of the covenant was found with anyone, and if anyone consented to the law, the sentence of the king put him to death.
verses.1:58: In their strength they kept doing so to Israel, to those who were found month by month in the cities.
verses.1:59: And on the twenty-fifth of the month they were offering sacrifices upon the altar that was on top of the altar.
verses.1:60: And according to the decree they put to death the women who had circumcised their children,
verses.1:61: and they hung the infants from their necks, and their households, and those who had circumcised them.
verses.1:62: And many in Israel were hanged. And they were fortified within themselves not to eat unclean things,
verses.1:63: and they chose to die, so that they would not be defiled by the foods and would not profane the holy covenant; and they died.
verses.1:64: And exceedingly great wrath came upon Israel.
verses.2:1: In those days Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarim, arose from Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
verses.2:2: And he had five sons: John, who was surnamed Gaddi;
verses.2:5: Eleazar, who was called Avaran; Jonathan, who was called Sapphus.
verses.2:6: And he saw the blasphemies that were taking place in Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.2:7: And he said, "Woe is me! Why was I born for this, to see the devastations of my people and the devastation of the holy city, and to sit there when it was given into the hand of enemies, the sanctuary into the hand of foreigners?
verses.2:8: Her temple has become like an honored man.
verses.2:9: The vessels of glory have been carried away captive; her infants have been killed in her streets, her young men by the sword of an enemy.
verses.2:10: What nation has not inherited palaces and has not seized her spoils?
verses.2:11: All her adornment has been taken away; instead of a free woman, she has become a slave.
verses.2:12: And look, our sanctuary and our beauty and our glory have been laid waste, and nations have profaned them.
verses.2:13: Why should we live any longer?"
verses.2:14: And Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, put on sackcloth, and mourned greatly.
verses.2:15: And those from the king who were enforcing the apostasy came to the city of Modein, so that they might sacrifice.
verses.2:16: And many from Israel came forward to them, and Mattathias and his sons gathered together.
verses.2:17: And those from the king answered and spoke to Mattathias, saying, "You are a ruler, honored and great in this city, and supported by sons and brothers.
verses.2:18: Now come forward first and carry out the command of the king, as all the nations have done, and the rulers of Judah, and those who were left in Jerusalem; and you and your house will be among the friends of the king, and you and your sons will be honored with silver and gold and many gifts."
verses.2:19: And Mattathias answered and said with a loud voice, "Even if all the nations that are in the house of the king's kingdom obey him, so that each one departs from the worship of his fathers, and have chosen his commands,
verses.2:20: yet I and my sons and my brothers—let us walk in the covenant of our fathers.
verses.2:21: Far be it from us to forsake law and ordinances.
verses.2:22: We will not obey the law of the king, to turn aside from our worship to the right or to the left."
verses.2:23: And when he finished speaking these words, a Jewish man came forward before the eyes of all to burn incense on the altar in Modein, according to the command of the king.
verses.2:24: And Mattathias saw it and became zealous, and his inward parts trembled, and he gave vent to wrath according to the judgment; and he ran and slaughtered him on the altar.
verses.2:25: And at that time he killed the king's man who was compelling them to sacrifice, and he tore down the altar.
verses.2:26: And he was zealous for the law, just as Phinehas did to Zimri son of Salom.
verses.2:27: And Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying, "Everyone who is zealous for the law and upholds the covenant, let him come out after me."
verses.2:28: And he and his sons fled to the mountains, and left behind all that they had in the city.
verses.2:29: Then many who were seeking righteousness and justice went down into the wilderness to settle there,
verses.2:30: they and their sons and their wives and their livestock, because the evils had become severe upon them.
verses.2:31: And it was reported to the king's men and to the forces that were in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had broken the command of the king had gone down into the hiding places in the wilderness.
verses.2:32: And many ran after them, and overtaking them, they encamped against them and drew up battle against them on the Sabbath day.
verses.2:33: And they said to them, "Enough now! Come out and do according to the word of the king, and you will live."
verses.2:34: And they said, "We will not come out, nor will we do the word of the king, to profane the Sabbath day."
verses.2:35: And they hastened battle against them.
verses.2:36: And they did not answer them, nor did they hurl a stone at them, nor did they block up the hiding places,
verses.2:37: saying, "Let us all die in our innocence; heaven and earth bear witness for us that you are destroying us unjustly."
verses.2:38: And they rose up against them in battle on the Sabbath, and they and their wives and their children and their livestock died, up to a thousand human souls.
verses.2:39: And Mattathias and his friends learned of it, and they mourned over them very greatly.
verses.2:40: And each man said to his neighbor, "If we all do as our brothers did and do not fight against the nations for our lives and our ordinances, they will now quickly destroy us from the earth."
verses.2:41: And they resolved on that day, saying, "Every man who comes against us to battle on the Sabbath day, let us fight against him, and we will certainly not all die, just as our brothers died in the hiding places."
verses.2:42: Then a company of Hasideans gathered to them with mighty force from Israel, everyone who offered himself willingly for the law.
verses.2:43: And all who were fleeing from the evils were added to them and became a support to them.
verses.2:44: And they organized a force and struck down sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath; and the rest fled to the nations to be saved.
verses.2:45: And Mattathias and his sons went around and tore down their altars,
verses.2:46: and they circumcised the uncircumcised boys, as many as he found within the borders of Israel, by force.
verses.2:47: And they pursued the sons of arrogance, and the work prospered in their hand.
verses.2:48: And they rescued the law from the hand of the nations and from the hand of the kings, and they did not give a horn to the sinner.
verses.2:49: And the days drew near for Mattathias to die, and he said to his sons, "Now arrogance and rebuke and a time of ruin and fierce wrath have grown strong.
verses.2:50: And now, children, be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
verses.2:51: Remember the deeds of our fathers, which they did in their generations, and receive great glory and eternal glory.
verses.2:52: Was not Abraham found faithful in testing, and righteousness was credited to him?
verses.2:53: Joseph, in the time of his distress, kept the commandment and became lord of Egypt.
verses.2:54: Phinehas our father, by being deeply zealous, received a covenant of a holy priesthood.
verses.2:55: Joshua, by fulfilling the word, became a judge in Israel.
verses.2:56: Caleb, by testifying to the assembly, received land as an inheritance.
verses.2:57: David, in his mercy, inherited a throne of an eternal kingdom.
verses.2:58: Elijah, by being deeply zealous for the law, was taken up, as it were, into heaven.
verses.2:59: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, by believing, were saved from the flame.
verses.2:60: Daniel, in his innocence, was rescued from the mouth of lions.
verses.2:61: And thus consider, generation by generation, that all who hope in Him will not grow weak.
verses.2:62: And do not be afraid of the words of a sinful man, because his glory is for dung and for worms.
verses.2:63: Today he will be lifted up, and he will certainly not be found, because he has returned to his dust, and his thought has perished.
verses.2:64: And you, children, be strong and courageous in your law, because in it you will be honored.
verses.2:65: And look, Simeon your brother, I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him all your days; he will be a father to you.
verses.2:66: And Judas Maccabeus himself, mighty in strength from his youth, he will be commander of the army for you, and you will fight the battle of the peoples.
verses.2:67: And you will bring to yourselves all the doers of the law, and execute the vengeance of your people.
verses.2:68: Repay recompense to the nations, and pay attention to the commands of the law."
verses.2:69: And he blessed them, and he was gathered to his fathers.
verses.2:70: And he died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year, and his sons buried him in the tombs of his fathers in Modein, and all Israel lamented for him with a great lamentation.
verses.3:1: And his son Judas, who was called Maccabeus, rose up in his place.
verses.3:2: And all his brothers and all who had joined his father helped him, and they fought the battle of Israel with gladness.
verses.3:3: And he extended glory for his people, and put on a breastplate like a giant, and strapped on his weapons of war; he waged battles, protecting the camp with a sword.
verses.3:4: And he was like a lion in his deeds, and like a young lion roaring for prey.
verses.3:5: And he pursued lawless men, searching them out, and set ablaze those who troubled his people.
verses.3:6: And the lawless shrank back from fear of him, and all the workers of lawlessness were thrown into turmoil, and deliverance prospered in his hand.
verses.3:7: And he embittered many kings, and made Jacob glad by his deeds, and forever his memory is for a blessing.
verses.3:8: And he passed through the cities of Judah, and utterly destroyed ungodly men upon it, and turned away wrath from Israel.
verses.3:9: And he became renowned to the end of the earth, and he gathered together those who were perishing.
verses.3:10: And Apollonius gathered nations, and from Samaria a great force, to fight against Israel.
verses.3:11: And Judas learned of it, and went out to meet him, and struck him and killed him; and many fell wounded, and the rest fled.
verses.3:12: And they took their equipment, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and he fought with it all his days.
verses.3:13: And Seron, the commander of the force of Syria, heard that Judas had mustered a company and an assembly of faithful men who were with him and going out to battle.
verses.3:14: And he said, "I will make a name for myself, and I will be glorified in the kingdom, and I will fight against Judas and those with him, and those who despise the word of the king."
verses.3:15: And he proceeded, and a strong army of ungodly men went up with him to help him, to execute vengeance on the sons of Israel.
verses.3:16: And he drew near to the ascent of Methoron, and Judas went out to meet him with very few men.
verses.3:17: Now when they saw the army coming to meet him, they said to Judas, "How will we, being so few, be able to fight against so great a multitude? And we ourselves are faint, having gone without food today."
verses.3:18: And Judas said, "It is easy for many to be shut up in the hands of a few, and there is no difference in the sight of Heaven to save by many or by few.
verses.3:19: For victory in battle is not in the size of a force, but rather strength is from Heaven.
verses.3:20: They come against us in an abundance of arrogance and lawlessness, to destroy us and our wives and our children, to plunder us.
verses.3:21: But we fight for our lives and our laws.
verses.3:22: And He Himself will crush them before our face; as for you, do not be afraid of them."
verses.3:23: Now when he finished speaking, he leaped upon them suddenly, and Seron and his army were crushed before him.
verses.3:24: And they pursued them down the descent of Beth-horon as far as the plain, and from among them about eight hundred men fell; and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
verses.3:25: And the fear of Judas and his brothers began, and terror fell upon the nations around them.
verses.3:26: And his name reached as far as the king, and every nation told of the battles of Judas.
verses.3:27: Now when King Antiochus heard these reports, he became enraged with fury, and he sent and gathered all the forces of his kingdom, an exceedingly strong army.
verses.3:28: And he opened his treasury and gave pay to his forces for the year, and he commanded them to be ready for every need for a year.
verses.3:29: And he saw that the silver had run out from the treasuries, and the tributes of the country were small because of the dissension and calamity that he had brought about in the land, to remove the laws that had been from the earliest days.
verses.3:30: And he feared that he would not have enough, as once and twice before, for the expenses and the gifts that he had previously given with a lavish hand.
verses.3:31: And he was greatly perplexed in his soul, and he resolved to go to Persia and to collect the tributes of the regions and to gather much silver.
verses.3:32: And he left Lysias, a distinguished man and of royal descent, over the affairs of the king from the river Euphrates as far as the borders of Egypt,
verses.3:33: and to raise his son Antiochus until he returned.
verses.3:34: And he handed over to him half of the forces and the elephants, and commanded him concerning everything that he wished, and concerning all those who inhabited Judea and Jerusalem,
verses.3:35: to send a force against them to cast out and destroy the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to remove its memory from the place,
verses.3:36: and to settle foreigners in all their borders, and to apportion their land by lot.
verses.3:37: And the king took the half of the forces that remained, and departed from Antioch, from the city of his kingdom, in the one hundred forty-seventh year; and he crossed the Euphrates River and traveled through the upper regions.
verses.3:38: And Lysias chose Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men from among the friends of the king.
verses.3:39: And he sent with them forty thousand men and seven thousand cavalry to go into the land of Judah and destroy it according to the word of the king.
verses.3:40: And they departed with all their force and came and encamped near Emmaus in the plain country.
verses.3:41: And the merchants of the country heard of their fame, and took a very great amount of silver and gold, and servants, and came into the camp to take the sons of Israel as servants; and forces of Syria and of the land of the foreigners joined them.
verses.3:42: And Judas and his brothers saw that evils had multiplied and that the forces would encamp within their borders; and they learned of the words of the kingdom that he had commanded to do to the people for destruction and complete ruin.
verses.3:43: And each one said to his neighbor, "Let us raise up the ruin of our people and of the sanctuary."
verses.3:44: And the congregation was assembled to be ready for battle, and to pray and ask for mercy and compassion.
verses.3:45: And Jerusalem was uninhabited like a wilderness; there was not one of her offspring going in or going out; and the sanctuary was trampled down, and sons of foreigners were in the citadel, a lodging place among the nations; and delight was taken away from Jacob, and flute and lyre ceased.
verses.3:46: And they gathered together and came to Mizpah, opposite Jerusalem, because formerly there was a place of prayer in Mizpah for Israel.
verses.3:47: And they fasted on that day, and put on sackcloth and put ashes on their heads, and tore their garments.
verses.3:48: And they spread open the book of the law concerning the things about which the nations were consulting the likenesses of their idols.
verses.3:49: And they brought the garments of the priesthood and the firstfruits and the tithes, and they raised up the Nazirites who had completed the days.
verses.3:50: And they cried out aloud to Heaven, saying, "What should we do with these, and where should we take them?
verses.3:51: And Your sanctuary has been trampled down and profaned, and Your priests are in mourning and humiliation.
verses.3:52: And look, the nations have gathered together against us to destroy us; You know what they plot against us.
verses.3:53: How will we be able to stand before their face, unless You help us?"
verses.3:54: And they sounded the trumpets and cried out with a loud voice.
verses.3:55: And after this Judas appointed leaders of the people: commanders of thousands, and commanders of hundreds, and commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.
verses.3:56: And he told those who were building a house, and those who were betrothed to wives, and those who were planting vineyards, and those who were fearful, to return, each one to his house, according to the law.
verses.3:57: And the army departed, and they encamped to the south of Emmaus.
verses.3:58: And Judas said, "Arm yourselves and be valiant men, and be ready for the morning to fight against these nations who have assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
verses.3:59: For it is better for us to die in battle than to look upon the evils of our nation and of the sanctuary.
verses.3:60: But as the will in Heaven may be, so He will do."
verses.4:1: And Gorgias took five thousand men and one thousand chosen cavalry, and the army set out by night,
verses.4:2: so as to fall upon the camp of the Jews and strike them suddenly; and the sons of the citadel were guides for him.
verses.4:3: And Judas heard of it, and he and the mighty men set out to strike the king's force that was in Emmaus,
verses.4:4: while the forces were still scattered away from the camp.
verses.4:5: And Gorgias came into the camp of Judas by night and found no one; and he was searching for them in the mountains, for he said, "These men are fleeing from us."
verses.4:6: And at daybreak Judas appeared in the plain with three thousand men; however, they did not have armor and sword as they wished.
verses.4:7: And they saw an army of nations, strong and clad in armor, and cavalry encircling it, and these were trained in war.
verses.4:8: And Judas said to the men who were with him, "Do not fear their multitude, and do not be terrified of their onslaught.
verses.4:9: Remember how our fathers were saved at the Red Sea, when Pharaoh pursued them with an army.
verses.4:10: And now let us cry out to Heaven, to see if He will favor us and remember the covenant of the fathers and crush this army before us today.
verses.4:11: And all the nations will know that there is One who redeems and saves Israel."
verses.4:12: And the foreigners lifted up their eyes and saw them close by, directly opposite,
verses.4:13: and they came out from the camp to battle; and those with Judas sounded the trumpets.
verses.4:14: And they joined battle, and the nations were crushed and fled into the plain.
verses.4:15: And all those in the rear fell by the sword; and they pursued them as far as Gazara and as far as the plains of Judea and Ashdod and Jamnia, and about three thousand men of them fell.
verses.4:16: And Judas and the force turned back from pursuing after them,
verses.4:17: and he said to the people, "Do not covet the spoils, for battle is directly before us,
verses.4:18: and Gorgias and the force are on the mountain near us. But stand now against our enemies and fight them, and after these things take spoils, and with boldness."
verses.4:19: While Judas was still finishing these things, a certain detachment appeared peering out from the mountain.
verses.4:20: And it saw that the army had been put to flight and that the camp was being burned; for the smoke that was seen made plain what had happened.
verses.4:21: And realizing these things, they were greatly terrified; and perceiving also the army of Judas in the plain ready for battle array,
verses.4:22: they all fled into the land of the foreigners.
verses.4:23: And Judas returned to the plundering of the camp; and he took gold and much silver, and blue and purple and sea-purple, and great wealth.
verses.4:24: And as they returned, they were singing hymns and blessing Heaven, "For His mercy is good forever."
verses.4:25: And there was a great salvation for Israel on that day.
verses.4:26: Now as many of the foreigners as escaped came and reported to Lysias all that had happened.
verses.4:27: And when he heard everything, he was dismayed and discouraged, because such things as he wished had not happened to Israel, and such things as the king had commanded him had not come to pass.
verses.4:28: And in the following year he mustered sixty thousand select men and five thousand cavalry, so as to subdue them.
verses.4:29: And they came into Idumea and encamped at Beth-zur, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
verses.4:30: And he saw that the army was strong, and he prayed and said, "Blessed are You, Savior of Israel, who crushed the onslaught of the mighty warrior by the hand of Your servant David, and You handed over the army of the foreigners into the hands of Jonathan son of Saul and his armor-bearer.
verses.4:31: Shut up this army in the hands of Your people Israel, and let them be put to shame over their force and their cavalry.
verses.4:32: Give them cowardice, and melt the audacity of their strength, and let them be shaken by their destruction.
verses.4:33: Strike them down by the sword of those who love You, and let all who have seen Your name praise You with hymns."
verses.4:34: And they clashed with one another, and about five thousand men fell from the army of Lysias, and they fell directly before them.
verses.4:35: Now when Lysias saw the rout that had happened to his division, and the courage that had come to that of Judas, and how they were ready either to live or to die nobly, he set out for Antioch; and he was recruiting mercenaries, so as to become even greater in number and come again into Judea.
verses.4:36: Now Judas and his brothers said, "Look, our enemies have been crushed; let us go up to cleanse the sanctuary and dedicate it."
verses.4:37: And the entire army was gathered together, and they went up to Mount Zion.
verses.4:38: And they saw our sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned down, and in the courts plants growing as in a forest or as on one of the mountains, and the chambers torn down.
verses.4:39: And they tore their garments, and lamented with a great lamentation, and put ashes on their heads.
verses.4:40: And they fell on their faces to the ground, and sounded the signal trumpets, and cried out to Heaven.
verses.4:41: Then Judas ordered men to fight those in the citadel until he cleansed the sanctuary.
verses.4:42: And he selected blameless priests who delighted in the law;
verses.4:43: and they cleansed the sanctuary and carried out the stones of defilement to an unclean place.
verses.4:44: And they took counsel concerning the altar of burnt offering that had been profaned, what they should do with it.
verses.4:45: And a good plan occurred to them, to tear it down, so that it would never become a reproach to them, because the nations had defiled it; and they tore down the altar.
verses.4:46: And they stored the stones on the mountain of the house in a suitable place, until a prophet should come to give an answer concerning them.
verses.4:47: And they took whole stones according to the law and built a new altar like the former one.
verses.4:48: And they built the sanctuary and the interior of the house, and he consecrated the courts.
verses.4:49: And they made the holy vessels new, and they brought the lampstand and the altar of burnt offerings and incense and the table into the temple.
verses.4:50: And they burned incense on the altar and lit the lamps that were on the lampstand, and they gave light in the temple.
verses.4:51: And they placed loaves on the table and hung the curtains; and they finished all the works that they had done.
verses.4:52: And they rose early in the morning on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, that is, the month of Chislev, of the one hundred and forty-eighth year.
verses.4:53: And they offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings that they had made.
verses.4:54: At the season, on the day on which the nations had profaned it, on that day it was dedicated with songs and lyres and harps and with cymbals.
verses.4:55: And all the people fell on their faces, and worshiped, and blessed Heaven, the One who had given them success.
verses.4:56: And they celebrated the dedication of the altar for eight days, and presented burnt offerings with gladness, and offered a sacrifice of deliverance and praise.
verses.4:57: And they adorned the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, and he renewed the gates and the chambers, and they fitted them with doors.
verses.4:58: And there was very great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the nations was turned away.
verses.4:59: And Judas and his brothers and all the assembly of Israel decreed that the days of dedication of the altar should be observed in their seasons year by year for eight days, from the twenty-fifth day of the month of Chislev, with gladness and joy.
verses.4:60: And at that time they built up Mount Zion with high walls and strong towers all around, so that the nations would never come and trample them down as they had done before.
verses.4:61: And they stationed a force there to guard it, and they fortified it to guard Beth-zur, so that the people might have a stronghold facing Idumea.
verses.5:1: And it happened, when the nations all around heard that the altar had been built and the sanctuary had been dedicated as before, that they became very angry.
verses.5:2: And they plotted to do away with the race of Jacob, those who were in their midst, and they began to put to death and to wipe out those among the people.
verses.5:3: And Judas waged war against the sons of Esau in Judea, at Akrabattene, because they were besieging Israel; and he struck them with a great blow, and subdued them, and took their plunder.
verses.5:4: And he remembered the wickedness of the sons of Baean, who were a snare and a stumbling block to the people by lying in ambush for them on the roads.
verses.5:5: And they were shut up by him in the towers, and he encamped against them, and devoted them to destruction, and burned its towers with fire along with all who were inside.
verses.5:6: And he crossed over against the sons of Ammon, and found a strong hand and a numerous people, and Timothy as their leader.
verses.5:7: And he engaged in many battles with them, and they were crushed before him, and he struck them down.
verses.5:8: And he seized Jaze and its daughters, and returned to Judea.
verses.5:9: And the nations that were in Gilead gathered together against Israel, those who were within their borders, to wipe them out; and they fled to Dathema, the fortress.
verses.5:10: And they sent letters to Judas and his brothers, saying, "The nations around us have gathered together against us to wipe us out,
verses.5:11: and they are preparing to come and seize the fortress into which we fled; and Timothy leads their army.
verses.5:12: Now therefore, come and deliver us from their hand, because a multitude of us has fallen.
verses.5:13: And all our brothers who were in the territory of Tubias have been put to death, and they have taken captive their wives and their children, along with their belongings, and they destroyed about one thousand men there."
verses.5:14: The letters were still being read, and look, other messengers arrived from Galilee, having torn their garments, reporting according to these words,
verses.5:15: saying, "Those from Ptolemais and Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners, have gathered together against them to annihilate us."
verses.5:16: Now when Judas and the people heard these words, a great assembly gathered together to deliberate on what they should do for their brothers who were in distress and being attacked by him.
verses.5:17: And Judas said to Simon his brother, "Choose men for yourself, and go and rescue your brothers in Galilee; while Jonathan my brother and I will go into Gilead."
verses.5:18: And he left Joseph the son of Zechariah, and Azariah, a leader of the people, with the remainder of the force in Judea for protection;
verses.5:19: and he commanded them, saying, "Take charge of this people, and do not engage in battle with the nations until we return."
verses.5:20: And three thousand men were allotted to Simon to go into Galilee, and to Judas, eight thousand men into Gilead.
verses.5:21: And Simon went into Galilee, and engaged in many battles with the nations; and the nations were crushed before him.
verses.5:22: And he pursued them as far as the cities of Ptolemais; and about three thousand men from the nations fell, and he took their plunder.
verses.5:23: And he took them from Galilee and in Arbacta, with the wives and the children and all that belonged to them, and they brought them into Judea with great gladness.
verses.5:24: And Judas Maccabeus and Jonathan his brother crossed the Jordan, and went a journey of three days in the wilderness.
verses.5:25: And they encountered the Nabataeans, who met them peacefully and recounted to them all the things that had happened to their brothers in Gilead,
verses.5:26: and that many of them have been shut up in Bozrah and Bosor, in Alama, Casphor, Makeb, and Carnaim; all these cities are fortified and large.
verses.5:27: And in the remaining cities of Gilead they have been shut up; for tomorrow they are set to encamp against the fortresses, and to capture them and wipe out all of them in one day.
verses.5:28: And Judas and his army suddenly turned onto the road into the wilderness to Bosor; and he captured the city, and killed every male by the edge of the sword, and took all their plunder, and burned it with fire.
verses.5:29: And he departed from there by night, and marched all the way to the fortress.
verses.5:30: And morning came, and they lifted up their eyes, and look, a numerous people of whom there was no number, carrying ladders and siege engines to capture the fortress; and they were attacking them.
verses.5:31: And Judas saw that the battle had begun, and the cry of the city went up to heaven with trumpets and a loud cry;
verses.5:32: and he said to the men of the force, "Fight today for our brothers."
verses.5:33: And he went out in three divisions from behind them; and he blew the trumpets, and they cried out in prayer.
verses.5:34: And the army of Timothy recognized that it was Maccabeus, and they fled from before him, and he struck them with a great blow; and about eight thousand men from among them fell on that day.
verses.5:35: And he turned aside to Maapha and fought against it, and captured it, and killed every male in it, and took its plunder, and burned it with fire.
verses.5:36: From there he departed and seized Chasphoth, Maked, Bosor, and the remaining cities of Gilead.
verses.5:37: Now after these things Timothy gathered another army, and encamped opposite Raphon on the other side of the stream.
verses.5:38: And Judas sent to spy out the camp; and they reported to him, saying, "All the nations around you have gathered together to them, a very large force.
verses.5:39: And Arabs have been hired to help them, and they are encamped on the other side of the stream, ready to come against you for battle." And Judas went to meet them.
verses.5:40: And Timothy said to the commanders of his force, as Judas and his army drew near to the stream of water, "If he crosses over to us first, we will not be able to withstand him, because he will surely prevail against us.
verses.5:41: But if he is afraid and encamps on the other side of the river, we will cross over to him."
verses.5:42: Now when Judas drew near to the stream of water, he stationed the scribes of the people by the stream, and commanded them, saying, "Do not allow any man to encamp, but let all come into the battle."
verses.5:43: And he crossed over to them first, and all his people in front of him; and all the nations were crushed before him, and they threw down all their weapons, and fled into the shrine in Carnaim.
verses.5:44: And they seized the city, and burned the shrine with fire along with all who were in it; and Carnaim was routed, and could no longer stand before Judas.
verses.5:45: Then Judas gathered all Israel, those who were in Gilead, from the least to the greatest, and their wives and their children and their belongings, a very great camp, to go into the land of Judah.
verses.5:46: And they came as far as Ephron, and this city was large, the one at the entrance, very strong; there was no way to turn aside from it to the right or to the left, but only to go through the middle of it.
verses.5:47: And those from the city shut them out, and blocked up the gates with stones.
verses.5:48: And Judas sent to them with peaceful words, saying, "I will pass through your land to go to our own land; and no one will harm you; only on foot will we pass through." And they were not willing to open to him.
verses.5:49: And Judas gave orders to proclaim in the camp that each one should encamp in the place where he was.
verses.5:50: And the men of the city encamped, and they fought against the city all that day and all the night, and the city was delivered into his hands.
verses.5:51: And he destroyed every male by the edge of the sword, and uprooted it, and took the plunder of the city, and passed through the city over those who had been killed.
verses.5:52: And they crossed the Jordan into the great plain opposite Beth-shan.
verses.5:53: And Judas kept gathering together those who were lagging behind and encouraging the people along the whole way, until he came into the land of Judah.
verses.5:54: And they went up to Mount Zion with gladness and joy. And they offered burnt offerings, because not one of them had fallen until they returned in peace.
verses.5:55: And in the days when Judas and Jonathan were in Gilead, and Simon his brother was in Galilee opposite Ptolemais,
verses.5:56: Joseph the son of Zechariah and Zechariah, commanders of the forces, heard of the brave deeds and of the warfare, what they had done;
verses.5:57: and they said, "We also will make a name for ourselves, and let us go to fight against the nations around us."
verses.5:58: And they gave orders to those of the force that was with them, and went against Jamnia.
verses.5:59: And Gorgias came out of the city, and his men, to meet them for battle.
verses.5:60: And Joseph and Azariah were routed, and they were pursued as far as the borders of Judea; and on that day about two thousand men from the people of Israel fell;
verses.5:61: and there was a great rout among the people, because they did not listen to Judas and his brothers, supposing that he would act bravely.
verses.5:62: But they were not of the seed of those men to whom the deliverance of Israel was given through their hand.
verses.5:63: And the man Judas and his brothers were greatly honored before all Israel and all the nations, wherever their name was heard;
verses.5:64: and they kept gathering together to them, praising them.
verses.5:65: And Judas and his brothers went out, and fought against the sons of Esau in the land toward the south, and he struck Hebron and its daughters; and he tore down its fortress, and burned its towers all around.
verses.5:66: And he departed to go into the land of the foreigners, and was passing through Samaria.
verses.5:67: On that day priests fell in battle while he wished to act bravely, when he went out into battle rashly.
verses.5:68: And Judas turned aside to Ashdod, the land of the foreigners, and tore down their altars, and burned up the carved images of their gods, and plundered the spoils of the cities, and returned to Judea.
verses.6:1: And King Antiochus was passing through the upper regions, and he heard that there was in Elymais in Persia a city renowned for wealth, silver, and gold;
verses.6:2: and the temple in it was exceedingly rich, and golden coverings, breastplates, and weapons were there, which Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian king, who first reigned over the Greeks, had left there.
verses.6:3: And he came and sought to capture the city and plunder it, but he was not able, because the matter became known to those of the city.
verses.6:4: And they rose up against him for battle, and he fled and departed from there with great grief to return to Babylon.
verses.6:5: And someone came to him in Persia reporting that the armies that had gone into the land of Judah had been routed,
verses.6:6: and Lysias had gone with a strong force at first and had been turned back from before them, and they had grown strong with the weapons they took from the armies they cut down;
verses.6:7: and they had torn down the abomination that he had built upon the altar in Jerusalem, and they had surrounded the sanctuary with high walls as before, and Beth-zur, his city.
verses.6:8: And it happened, when the king heard these words, he was astounded and greatly shaken; and he fell onto his bed and fell into sickness from grief, because it had not turned out for him as he had planned.
verses.6:9: And he was there many days, because great grief was renewed upon him, and he concluded that he was dying.
verses.6:10: And he called all his friends and said to them, "Sleep departs from my eyes, and my heart has collapsed from anxiety.
verses.6:11: And I said to my heart, 'To what distress have I come, and to what a great flood, in which I now am? For I was kind and beloved in my authority.'
verses.6:12: But now I remember the evils that I did in Jerusalem; and I took all the silver and gold vessels that were in it, and I sent to destroy the inhabitants of Judah without cause.
verses.6:13: I know that on account of these things these evils have found me; and look, I am perishing from great grief in a foreign land."
verses.6:14: And he called Philip, one of his friends, and appointed him over all his kingdom.
verses.6:15: And he gave him the diadem, his robe, and the signet ring, to guide Antiochus his son and raise him to reign.
verses.6:16: And King Antiochus died there in the one hundred forty-ninth year.
verses.6:17: And Lysias learned that the king was dead, and he appointed Antiochus his son, whom he had raised while young, to reign in his place, and he called his name Eupator.
verses.6:18: And those from the citadel were hemming Israel in around the sanctuary, continually seeking evil, and they were a support for the nations.
verses.6:19: And Judas resolved to destroy them, and he assembled all the people to besiege them
verses.6:20: in the one hundred fiftieth year; and he built siege mounds and siege engines against them.
verses.6:21: And they went out from it, from the blockade, and some of the ungodly from Israel joined them.
verses.6:22: And they went to the king and said, "How long will you not execute justice and avenge our brothers?
verses.6:23: We were pleased to serve your father, and to walk by the things spoken by him, and to follow his decrees;
verses.6:24: for on account of this, those of our people became estranged from us; moreover, as many of us as were found were put to death, and our inheritances were plundered.
verses.6:25: And they did not stretch out a hand against us only, but also against all their borders.
verses.6:26: And look, today they have encamped against the citadel in Jerusalem to capture it, and they have fortified the sanctuary and Beth-zur.
verses.6:27: And if you do not forestall them quickly, they will do greater things than these, and you will not be able to restrain them."
verses.6:28: And the king became angry when he heard; and he gathered all his friends, commanders of his force, and those in charge of the reins.
verses.6:29: And from other kings and from islands of the seas, mercenary forces came to him.
verses.6:30: And the number of his forces was one hundred thousand foot soldiers, and twenty thousand horses, and thirty-two elephants skilled in war.
verses.6:31: And they came through Idumea, and encamped against Beth-zur, and fought for many days, and built siege engines; and they went out and burned them with fire, and fought courageously.
verses.6:32: And Judas departed from the citadel and encamped at Beth-zechariah, opposite the camp of the king.
verses.6:33: And the king rose early in the morning and moved the army in its rush along the road to Beth-zechariah, and the forces were drawn up for battle, and they sounded the trumpets.
verses.6:34: And they showed the elephants the blood of grapes and mulberries, to rouse them for battle.
verses.6:35: And they distributed the beasts among the phalanxes, and they stationed beside each elephant one thousand men armored in chain mail, and bronze helmets were on their heads; and five hundred chosen cavalry were assigned to each beast.
verses.6:36: These were there beforehand, wherever the beast was; and wherever it went, they went together; they did not leave it.
verses.6:37: And strong, covered wooden towers were upon them, on each beast, strapped onto them with contrivances; and upon each were thirty-two men who fought upon them, and its Indian.
verses.6:38: And he stationed the remaining cavalry on this side and on that, on the two sides of the army, striking terror and being protected among the phalanxes.
verses.6:39: And when the sun shone upon the golden shields, the mountains shone from them and blazed like torches of fire.
verses.6:40: And part of the army of the king was spread out upon the high mountains, and some upon the low ground; and they advanced steadily and in order.
verses.6:41: And all who heard the sound of their multitude, and the marching of the multitude, and the clashing of the weapons were shaken. For the army was exceedingly great and strong.
verses.6:42: And Judas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men from the army of the king fell.
verses.6:43: And Eleazar Sauaran saw one of the beasts armored with royal breastplates, and it towered above all the beasts, and it appeared that the king was on it.
verses.6:44: And he gave himself to save his people and to acquire for himself an eternal name.
verses.6:45: And he ran at it boldly into the middle of the phalanx, and he killed to the right and to the left, and they parted from him this way and that.
verses.6:46: And he slipped under the elephant, and thrust beneath it and killed it; and it fell to the ground upon him, and he died there.
verses.6:47: And they saw the strength of the kingdom and the onslaughts of the forces, and they turned away from them.
verses.6:48: And from the army of the king they went up to Jerusalem to meet them, and the king encamped in Judea and at Mount Zion.
verses.6:49: And he dealt with those of Beth-zur; and he went out from the city, because they had no provisions there to be shut up in it, because it was a sabbath for the land.
verses.6:50: And the king captured Beth-zur and stationed a garrison there to guard it.
verses.6:51: And he encamped against the sanctuary for many days, and he set up there siege mounds and siege engines, and fire-throwers and stone-throwers, and scorpions to shoot arrows, and slings.
verses.6:52: And they also built siege engines against their siege engines, and they fought for many days.
verses.6:53: But there was no food in the sanctuary, because it was the seventh year, and those who had been rescued into Judea from the nations had eaten up the remainder of the supplies;
verses.6:54: and few men were left in the sanctuary, because the famine prevailed over them; and they scattered, each to his own place.
verses.6:55: And Lysias heard that Philip, whom King Antiochus while still alive had appointed to raise Antiochus his son to reign,
verses.6:56: had returned from Persia and Media, and with him the forces of the king that had gone out, and that he was seeking to take over the affairs of state.
verses.6:57: And they hastened and were spurred on to depart; and he said to the king and the leaders of the force and the men, "We are failing day by day, and we have little food, and the place where we are encamped is strong, and the affairs of the kingdom press upon us.
verses.6:58: Now therefore let us give the right hand to these people, and let us make peace with them and with all their nation;
verses.6:59: and let us grant them to walk by their laws as before; for on account of their laws, which we abolished, they became angry and did all these things."
verses.6:60: And the word was pleasing before the king and the commanders, and he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted.
verses.6:61: And the king and the commanders swore to them upon these terms; he went out from the stronghold,
verses.6:62: and the king entered Mount Zion, and saw the fortification of the place; and he broke the oath that he had sworn, and gave orders and tore down the wall all around.
verses.6:63: And they departed in haste, and he returned to Antioch, and he found Philip in control of the city; and he fought against him and captured the city by force.
verses.7:1: In the fifty-first year, Demetrius the son of Seleucus went out from Rome and went up with a few men to a coastal city, and reigned there.
verses.7:2: And it happened that as he was entering the royal house of his fathers, the forces seized Antiochus and Lysias to bring them to him.
verses.7:3: And the matter became known to him, and he said, "Do not show me their faces."
verses.7:4: And the forces killed them, and Demetrius sat on the throne of his kingdom.
verses.7:5: And all the lawless and ungodly men from Israel came to him, and Alcimus was leading them, wanting to serve as priest.
verses.7:6: And they accused the people to the king, saying, "Judas and his brothers have destroyed all your friends, and he has scattered us from our land.
verses.7:7: Now therefore, send a man whom you trust, and let him go and see all the destruction that he has done to us and to the king's country, and he has punished them and all those who help them."
verses.7:8: And the king chose Bacchides, one of the king's friends, who was ruling in the region beyond the River, and was great in the kingdom and faithful to the king.
verses.7:9: And he sent him and Alcimus the ungodly, and they established the priesthood for him, and he commanded him to carry out the vengeance on the sons of Israel.
verses.7:10: And he departed and came with a large force into the land of Judah; and he sent messengers to Judas and to his brothers with peaceful words, deceitfully.
verses.7:11: And they did not pay attention to their words, for they saw that they had come with a large force.
verses.7:12: And an assembly of scribes gathered together to Alcimus and Bacchides to seek what was just.
verses.7:13: And the Hasideans were the first among the sons of Israel, and they sought peace from them;
verses.7:14: for they said, "A man who is a priest from the seed of Aaron has come with the forces, and he will not wrong us."
verses.7:15: And he spoke peaceful words with them and swore to them, saying, "We will not seek evil against you or your friends."
verses.7:16: And they trusted him, and he seized sixty men from among them and killed them in one day, according to the words that he wrote:
verses.7:17: "The flesh of Your godly ones and their blood they poured out around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
verses.7:18: And fear of them and trembling fell upon all the people, because they said, "There is no truth or justice in them, for they have violated the agreement and the oath that they swore."
verses.7:19: And Bacchides set out from Jerusalem and encamped at Bezeth, and he sent and seized many of the men with him who had deserted, and some of the people, and slaughtered them into the great cistern.
verses.7:20: And he committed the country to Alcimus and left a force with him to help him; and Bacchides departed to the king.
verses.7:21: And Alcimus contended for the high priesthood.
verses.7:22: And all those who were troubling their people gathered to him, and they gained control of the land of Judah and inflicted a great blow in Israel.
verses.7:23: And Judas saw all the evil that Alcimus and those with him had done among the sons of Israel, more than the nations;
verses.7:24: and he went out into all the territory of Judea and all around, and carried out vengeance on the men and on those who had deserted, and they were restrained from going into the country.
verses.7:25: Now when Alcimus saw that Judas and those with him had grown strong, and knew that he was able to withstand them, he returned to the king and accused them of wicked things.
verses.7:26: And the king sent Nicanor, one of his honored officials and one who hated and was hostile to Israel, and he commanded him to wipe out the people.
verses.7:27: And Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a large force, and sent to Judas and his brothers deceitfully with peaceful words, saying,
verses.7:28: "Let there be no fighting between me and you; I will come with a few men so that I may see your faces in peace."
verses.7:29: And he came to Judas, and they greeted one another peacefully; and the enemies were ready to snatch Judas away.
verses.7:30: And the matter became known to Judas, that he had come against him deceitfully; and he was alarmed because of him, and did not want to see his face again.
verses.7:31: And Nicanor knew that his plan had been revealed, and he went out to meet Judas near Charpharsarama.
verses.7:32: And about five thousand men of those with Nicanor fell, and they fled into the city of David.
verses.7:33: And after these things Nicanor went up to Mount Zion; and some of the priests came out from the sanctuary, and some of the elders of the people, to greet him peacefully and to show him the burnt offering that was being offered on behalf of the king.
verses.7:34: And he mocked them, and laughed at them, and defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
verses.7:35: And he swore in fury, saying, "Unless Judas and his army are handed over into my hands right now, then it will be that if I return in peace, I will burn down this house." And he went out in fury.
verses.7:36: And the priests went in and stood before the altar and the temple, and wept and said,
verses.7:37: "You chose this house for Your name to be called upon it, to be a house of prayer and supplication for Your people.
verses.7:38: Carry out vengeance on this man and on his army, and let them fall by the sword; remember their blasphemies, and do not grant them survival."
verses.7:39: And Nicanor went out from Jerusalem, and they encamped at Beth-horon, and a force from Syria met him.
verses.7:40: And Judas encamped at Adasa with three thousand men; and Judas prayed and said,
verses.7:41: "When those from the king blasphemed, Your angel went out and struck down among them one hundred and eighty-five thousand.
verses.7:42: In the same way, crush this army before us today; and let the rest know that he spoke evil against Your sanctuary, and judge him according to his evil."
verses.7:43: And the armies joined in battle on the thirteenth of the month of Adar, and Nicanor's army was crushed; and he himself fell first in the battle.
verses.7:44: Now when his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
verses.7:45: And they pursued them a day's journey, from Adasa until they came to Gazara, and they sounded the signal trumpets behind them.
verses.7:46: And people came out from all the villages of Judea all around and outflanked them, and these turned back toward those; and they all fell by the sword, and not even one of them was left.
verses.7:47: And they took the spoils and the plunder, and they cut off Nicanor's head and his right hand, which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought them and stretched them out beside Jerusalem.
verses.7:48: And the people rejoiced greatly, and they observed that day as a great day of gladness.
verses.7:49: And they decreed to observe this day every year on the thirteenth of Adar.
verses.7:50: And the land of Judah had rest for a few days.
verses.8:1: Now Judas heard the name of the Romans, that they are mighty in strength, and that they are well pleased with all who have joined themselves to them, and that with as many as join themselves to them, and as many as approach them, they establish friendship,
verses.8:2: and that they are mighty in strength. And they recounted to him their wars and the valiant deeds that they perform among the Gauls, and that they gained control over them and brought them under tribute;
verses.8:3: and all that they did in the territory of Spain, to gain control of the mines of silver and gold there,
verses.8:4: and they gained control of the entire place by their counsel and patience (and the place was very far away from them), and of the kings who came against them from the end of the earth, until they crushed them and struck them with a great blow, and the rest pay them tribute year by year;
verses.8:5: and Philip, and Perseus king of the Kittim, and those who had risen up against them, they crushed in war and gained control over them;
verses.8:6: and Antiochus, the great king of Asia, who went against them to war having one hundred and twenty elephants, and cavalry, and chariots, and a very great force, was crushed by them;
verses.8:7: and they took him alive, and established for them that both he and those who would reign after him should pay a great tribute, and give hostages and a settlement,
verses.8:8: and the territory of India, and Media, and Lydia, and some of their finest territories; and having taken them from him, they gave them to King Eumenes;
verses.8:9: and that those from Greece planned to come and destroy them,
verses.8:10: and the matter became known to them, and they sent one general against them, and they waged war against them, and many of them fell wounded, and they took captive their wives and their children, and plundered them, and gained control of their land, and tore down their strongholds, and plundered them, and enslaved them to this day.
verses.8:11: And the remaining kingdoms and the islands, as many as ever rose up against them, they destroyed and enslaved to themselves; but with their friends and those who relied on them they maintained friendship,
verses.8:12: and they gained control of the kingdoms near and far; and as many as heard their name were afraid of them.
verses.8:13: Those whom they wish to help and to make kings will reign, and those whom they wish, they depose; and they were greatly exalted.
verses.8:14: Yet in all these things not one of them put on a diadem, nor did they clothe themselves in purple so as to be magnified by it.
verses.8:15: And they made a council chamber for themselves, and every day three hundred and twenty deliberated, taking counsel continually concerning the people, so as to keep themselves in good order.
verses.8:16: And they trust one man to rule over them year by year and to have dominion over all their land, and all obey that one, and there is neither envy nor jealousy among them.
verses.8:17: And Judas chose Eupolemus son of John, son of Hakkoz, and Jason son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to establish friendship and an alliance with them,
verses.8:18: and to remove their yoke, because they saw the kingdom of the Greeks enslaving Israel in bondage.
verses.8:19: And they went to Rome, and the journey was very long; and they entered the council chamber and spoke:
verses.8:20: "Judas, who is also called Maccabeus, and his brothers and the people of the Jews sent us to you to establish an alliance and peace with you, and for us to be enrolled as your allies and friends."
verses.8:21: And the proposal was pleasing before them.
verses.8:22: And this is the copy of the document which they wrote in reply on bronze tablets and sent to Jerusalem to be there with them as a memorial of peace and alliance:
verses.8:23: "May it go well with the Romans and with the nation of the Jews at sea and on land forever, and may sword and enemy be kept far from them.
verses.8:24: Now if war comes first to Rome or to any of their allies in all their dominion,
verses.8:25: the nation of the Jews will fight as allies, as the occasion may be prescribed for them, with a full heart.
verses.8:26: And to those waging war they will neither give nor supply grain, weapons, silver, or ships, as it seemed good to Rome; and they will keep their obligations, receiving nothing.
verses.8:27: And in the same way, if war happens first to the nation of the Jews, the Romans will fight as allies from the soul, as the occasion may prescribe for them.
verses.8:28: And to those fighting as allies no grain, weapons, or silver will be given, as it seemed good to Rome; and they will keep these obligations, and not with deceit.
verses.8:29: According to these terms, the Romans thus established it with the people of the Jews.
verses.8:30: Now if, after these terms, both parties decide to add or to take away, they will act by their own choice, and whatever they add or take away will be binding.
verses.8:31: And concerning the evils that King Demetrius is committing against them, we have written to him, saying, 'Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends, our allies, the Jews?
verses.8:32: If, therefore, they appeal against you again, we will execute justice for them, and we will wage war against you by sea and by land.'"
verses.9:1: And Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his forces had made war, and he proceeded to send Bacchides and Alcimus a second time into the land of Judah, and the right wing with them.
verses.9:2: And they went along the road to Gilgal, and they encamped against Messaloth, which is in Arbela, and captured it, and he destroyed many human lives.
verses.9:3: And in the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year, they encamped at Jerusalem.
verses.9:4: And they set out and went to Berea with twenty thousand men and two thousand horses.
verses.9:5: And Judas was encamped at Alasa, and three thousand chosen men were with him.
verses.9:6: And they saw the multitude of the forces, that they were many, and they were greatly afraid; and many slipped away from the camp; none of them were left except eight hundred men.
verses.9:7: And Judas saw that his camp had melted away, and the battle was pressing him; and he was crushed in heart, because he had no time to gather them together.
verses.9:8: And he grew faint, and he said to those who were left, "Let us rise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we may be able to fight them."
verses.9:9: And they tried to turn him back, saying, "We will by no means be able; rather, let us save our own lives for now. Let us return with our brothers and fight against them; for we are few."
verses.9:10: And Judas said, "Far be it from me to do this thing, to flee from them; and our time has drawn near, and let us die with courage for the sake of our brothers, and let us not leave a reproach against our glory."
verses.9:11: And the force set out from the camp, and they took their stand to meet them, and the cavalry was divided into two divisions, and the slingers and the archers went ahead of the force, and the front-line fighters, all the mighty men.
verses.9:12: Now Bacchides was on the right wing, and the phalanx drew near from the two sides, and they were sounding the trumpets; and those on Judas's side themselves also blew the trumpets.
verses.9:13: And the earth was shaken by their camps, and the battle was joined from morning until evening.
verses.9:14: And Judas saw that Bacchides and the strength of the camp were on the right, and all those courageous in heart came together with him.
verses.9:15: And the right wing was crushed by them, and he pursued after them as far as the mountain of Ashdod.
verses.9:16: And those on the left wing saw that the right wing was crushed, and they turned close on the heels of Judas and those with him from the rear.
verses.9:17: And the battle grew heavy, and many fell wounded from one side and the other.
verses.9:18: And Judas fell, and the rest fled.
verses.9:19: And Jonathan and Simon took up Judas his brother and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.
verses.9:20: And they wept for him there, and all Israel lamented him with a great lamentation, and they mourned for many days and said,
verses.9:21: "How a mighty man has fallen, who saved Israel!"
verses.9:22: And the rest of the acts of Judas, and of the wars and the valiant deeds that he did, and of his greatness, were not written down, for they were very many.
verses.9:23: And it came about after the death of Judas that the lawless emerged in all the borders of Israel, and all those who practiced unrighteousness sprang up.
verses.9:24: In those days there was a very great famine, and the country defected with them.
verses.9:25: And Bacchides chose the ungodly men and appointed them lords of the country.
verses.9:26: And they sought and searched out the friends of Judas and brought them to Bacchides; and he took vengeance on them, and they mocked them.
verses.9:27: And there was great distress in Israel, such as had not occurred since the day no prophet appeared to them.
verses.9:28: And all the friends of Judas assembled and said to Jonathan,
verses.9:29: "Since your brother Judas has died, there is no man like him to go out against the enemies and Bacchides, and against those who are hostile to our nation.
verses.9:30: Now therefore, we have chosen you today to be in his place as ruler and leader for us, to fight our battle."
verses.9:31: And Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time, and he rose up in place of Judas his brother.
verses.9:32: And Bacchides learned of it, and he sought to kill him.
verses.9:33: And Jonathan and Simon his brother and all those with him learned of it, and they fled into the wilderness of Tekoa and encamped by the water of the cistern of Asphal.
verses.9:34: And Bacchides learned of it on the Sabbath day, and he himself and all his army came across the Jordan.
verses.9:35: And he sent his brother as leader of the crowd, and he appealed to the Nabataeans, his friends, that he might deposit their abundant baggage with them.
verses.9:36: And the sons of Jambrin came out from Medeba and seized John and all that he had, and they went away with them.
verses.9:37: Now after these things, they reported to Jonathan and to Simon his brother, "The sons of Jambrin are holding a great wedding and are bringing the bride from Nadabath, the daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan, with a great escort."
verses.9:38: And they remembered John their brother, and they went up and hid under the cover of the mountain.
verses.9:39: And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and look, there was a tumult and much baggage; and the bridegroom came out, and his friends and his brothers, to meet them with tambourines and musical instruments and many weapons.
verses.9:40: And they rose up against them from the ambush and killed them; and many fell wounded, and the rest fled to the mountain, and they took all their goods.
verses.9:41: And the wedding was turned into mourning, and the sound of their musical instruments into a lament.
verses.9:42: And they took vengeance for the blood of their brother, and they returned to the mountain of the Jordan.
verses.9:43: And Bacchides heard of it, and he came on the Sabbath day as far as the banks of the Jordan with a great force.
verses.9:44: And Jonathan said to his brothers, "Let us rise now and fight for our lives, for today is not like yesterday and the day before.
verses.9:45: For look, the battle is in front of us and behind us, and the water of the Jordan is on this side and on that, and marsh and thicket, and there is no place to turn aside.
verses.9:46: Now therefore, cry out to Heaven, so that you may be delivered from the hand of our enemies."
verses.9:47: And the battle was joined, and Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but he turned aside backward away from him.
verses.9:48: And Jonathan and those with him leaped into the Jordan and swam across to the other side, and they did not cross the Jordan against them.
verses.9:49: And about a thousand men fell on Bacchides's side on that day.
verses.9:50: And they returned to Jerusalem and built fortified cities in Judea: the fortress that is in Jericho, and Emmaus, and Beth-horon, and Bethel, and Thamnatha Pharathon, and Tephon, with high walls and gates and bars.
verses.9:51: And they placed a garrison in them to be hostile to Israel.
verses.9:52: And they fortified the city, and Beth-zur, and Gazara, and the citadel, and they placed in them forces and stores of food.
verses.9:53: And they took the sons of the leaders of the country as hostages, and they placed them in the citadel in Jerusalem in custody.
verses.9:54: And in the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alcimus gave orders to tear down the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary, and he tore down the works of the prophets, and he began the tearing down.
verses.9:55: At that time Alcimus was struck, and his works were hindered, and his mouth was shut, and he was paralyzed, and he was no longer able to speak a word or to give instructions concerning his house.
verses.9:56: And Alcimus died at that time with great torment.
verses.9:57: And Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died, and he returned to the king, and the land of Judah was quiet for two years.
verses.9:58: And all the lawless took counsel, saying, "Look, Jonathan and those on his side are dwelling in quietness, confident; now therefore, we will bring Bacchides, and he will seize them all in one night."
verses.9:59: And they went and took counsel with him.
verses.9:60: And he set out to come with a great force, and he sent letters secretly to all his allies who were in Judea, so that they might seize Jonathan and those with him; and he was not able, because their plan became known to them.
verses.9:61: And they seized from the men of the country, the ringleaders of the wickedness, about fifty men, and he killed them.
verses.9:62: And Jonathan and Simon and those with him withdrew to Bethbasi, which is in the wilderness, and he rebuilt the parts of it that had been torn down and strengthened it.
verses.9:63: And Bacchides learned of it and gathered together all his multitude, and he sent orders to those from Judea.
verses.9:64: And he came and encamped against Bethbasi, and he fought against it for many days and made siege engines.
verses.9:65: And Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city and went out into the country, and he came with a small number.
verses.9:66: And he struck Odomera and his brothers and the sons of Phasiron in their encampment, and he began to strike and to go up with the forces.
verses.9:67: And Simon and those with him went out from the city and burned the siege engines.
verses.9:68: And they fought against Bacchides, and he was crushed by them, and they pressed him greatly, because his plan and his expedition were in vain.
verses.9:69: And they were enraged with fury against the lawless men who had counseled him to come into the country, and they killed many of them; and he planned to depart to his own land.
verses.9:70: And Jonathan learned of it, and he sent envoys to him to conclude peace with him and to restore the captives to them.
verses.9:71: And he accepted and did according to his words, and he swore to him not to seek harm against him all the days of his life.
verses.9:72: And he restored to him the captives whom he had previously taken captive from the land of Judah; and he turned back and departed to his own land, and he did not come again into their borders.
verses.9:73: And the sword ceased from Israel, and Jonathan settled in Michmash; and Jonathan began to judge the people, and he destroyed the ungodly from Israel.
verses.10:1: And in the one hundred and sixtieth year, Alexander Epiphanes, the son of Antiochus, went up and seized Ptolemais, and they received him, and he reigned there.
verses.10:2: And King Demetrius heard of it, and gathered very numerous forces, and went out to meet him for war.
verses.10:3: And Demetrius sent letters to Jonathan with peaceful words, so as to magnify him.
verses.10:4: For he said, "Let us act first to make peace with them before he makes peace with Alexander against us.
verses.10:5: For he will remember all the evils that we perpetrated against him, and against his brothers, and against his nation."
verses.10:6: And he gave him authority to gather forces, and to prepare weapons, and for him to be his ally; and he ordered that the hostages who were in the citadel be handed over to him.
verses.10:7: And Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters in the hearing of all the people and of those from the citadel.
verses.10:8: And they feared with a great fear when they heard that the king had given them authority to gather forces.
verses.10:9: And those from the citadel handed over the hostages to Jonathan, and they returned them to their parents.
verses.10:10: And Jonathan settled in Jerusalem, and began to build and renew the city.
verses.10:11: And he told those who were doing the work to build the walls and Mount Zion all around with squared stones for fortification, and they did so.
verses.10:12: And the foreigners who were in the strongholds that Bacchides had built fled.
verses.10:13: And each one left his place and departed to his own land.
verses.10:14: Only in Beth-zur were some of those who had abandoned the law and the ordinances left behind, for it was a place of refuge for them.
verses.10:15: And King Alexander heard of all the promises that Demetrius had sent to Jonathan, and they recounted to him the wars and the brave deeds that he and his brothers had done, and the hardships that they had endured.
verses.10:16: And he said, "Will we find even one man like this? And now, let us make him our friend and ally."
verses.10:17: And he wrote letters and sent them to him according to these words, saying:
verses.10:18: "King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
verses.10:19: We have heard about you, that you are a man excellent in strength and fit to be our friend.
verses.10:20: And now we have appointed you today as high priest of your nation, and to be called Friend of the King" (and they sent him a purple robe and a golden crown) "and to take our side and keep friendship with us."
verses.10:21: And Jonathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Feast of Booths, and he gathered forces and prepared many weapons.
verses.10:22: And Demetrius heard these words, and was grieved, and said,
verses.10:23: "What is this that we have done, that Alexander has gotten ahead of us in securing friendship with the Jews for support?
verses.10:24: I also will write to them words of encouragement and exaltation and gifts, so that they may be with me for help."
verses.10:25: And he sent to them according to these words: "King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.10:26: Since you kept the agreements with us, and remained in our friendship, and did not go over to our enemies, we heard and rejoiced.
verses.10:27: And now continue still to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good things in return for what you do with us.
verses.10:28: And we will grant you many remissions, and we will give you gifts.
verses.10:29: And now I release you and exempt all the Jews from the tributes, and from the price of salt, and from the crowns.
verses.10:30: And instead of the third of the sown crop, and instead of the half of the fruit of the trees that falls to me to receive, I remit from today and onward taking them from the land of Judah and from the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
verses.10:31: And let Jerusalem be holy and exempt, and its borders, the tithes and the taxes.
