verses.10:32: I also relinquish authority over the citadel that is in Jerusalem, and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men whom he himself may choose, to guard it.
verses.10:33: And every soul of the Jews who was taken captive from the land of Judah into all my kingdom I release free without payment; and let all remit the tributes even of their livestock.
verses.10:34: And all the feasts and the Sabbaths and new moons and appointed days, and three days before a feast and three days after a feast, let all the days be days of exemption and release for all the Jews who are in all my kingdom.
verses.10:35: And no one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
verses.10:36: And let there be enrolled from the Jews into the forces of the king up to thirty thousand men, and allowances shall be given to them as is due to all the forces of the king.
verses.10:37: And some of them shall be stationed in the great strongholds of the king, and some of these shall be appointed over offices of the kingdom that require trust; and let those over them and the commanders be from among them, and let them walk by their own laws, just as the king has also commanded in the land of Judah.
verses.10:38: And as for the three districts that have been added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be added to Judea so as to be reckoned as being under one ruler, so as not to obey any other authority except the high priest.
verses.10:39: Ptolemais and the territory adjoining it I have given as a gift to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, for the proper expense of the sanctuary.
verses.10:40: And I also give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the accounts of the king, from the appropriate places.
verses.10:41: And all the surplus that they were not paying out from the offices, as in the former years, from now on they shall give for the works of the house.
verses.10:42: And in addition to these, five thousand shekels of silver, which they used to take from the offices, as in the former years, from the account of the sanctuary every year, these also are remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
verses.10:43: And as many as flee to the temple in Jerusalem and within all its borders, being liable for royal dues or any matter, let them be released, along with everything that belongs to them in my kingdom.
verses.10:44: And for the building and renewing of the works of the sanctuary, the expense also shall be given from the account of the king.
verses.10:45: And for the building of the walls of Jerusalem and fortifying it all around, the expense also shall be given from the account of the king, and for building the walls in Judea."
verses.10:46: Now when Jonathan and the people heard these words, he did not believe them, nor did they receive them, because they remembered the great evil that he had done in Israel, and how he had afflicted them greatly.
verses.10:47: And they were well pleased with Alexander, because he had become to them the originator of peaceful words, and they fought as allies with him all the days.
verses.10:48: And King Alexander gathered great forces and encamped opposite Demetrius.
verses.10:49: And the two kings joined battle, and the army of Demetrius fled, and Alexander pursued him and prevailed over them.
verses.10:50: And he pressed the battle fiercely until the sun went down, and Demetrius fell on that day.
verses.10:51: And Alexander sent envoys to Ptolemy, king of Egypt, according to these words, saying:
verses.10:52: "Since I have returned to my kingdom, and sat on the throne of my fathers, and gained control of the rule, and crushed Demetrius, and gained mastery over our country;
verses.10:53: and I joined battle with him, and he and his army were crushed by us, and we sat on the throne of his kingdom;
verses.10:54: and let us establish friendship with him; and now give me your daughter as a wife, and I will make a marriage alliance with you, and I will give gifts to you and to her worthy of you."
verses.10:55: And King Ptolemy answered, saying, "Good is the day on which you returned to the land of your fathers and sat on the throne of their kingdom.
verses.10:56: And now I will do for you what you have written; but meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will make a marriage alliance with you just as you have said."
verses.10:57: And Ptolemy went out from Egypt, he and his daughter Cleopatra, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
verses.10:58: And King Alexander met him, and he gave him his daughter Cleopatra in marriage, and celebrated her wedding in Ptolemais, as kings do, with great splendor.
verses.10:59: And King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come to meet him.
verses.10:60: And he went with splendor to Ptolemais and met the two kings; and he gave them silver and gold, and to their friends also, and many gifts, and he found favor before them.
verses.10:61: And pestilent men from Israel, lawless men, gathered against him to bring charges against him; and the king paid no attention to them.
verses.10:62: And the king commanded them, and he removed Jonathan's garments and clothed him with a purple robe; and they did so.
verses.10:63: And the king seated him with him, and said to his officials, "Go out with him into the middle of the city, and proclaim that no one is to bring charges against this man concerning any matter, and let no one trouble him for any reason."
verses.10:64: And it happened, when those who were bringing charges saw his honor as he proclaimed it, and him clothed in fine linen, that they all fled.
verses.10:65: And the king honored him, and enrolled him among the First Friends, and made him general and district governor.
verses.10:66: And Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with peace and gladness.
verses.10:67: And in the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius, the son of Demetrius, came from Crete to the land of his fathers.
verses.10:68: And King Alexander heard of it, and was exceedingly grieved, and returned to Antioch.
verses.10:69: And Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria, and he gathered a great force and encamped at Jamnia.
verses.10:70: And he sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying, "You all alone lift yourself up against us, and I have become a laughingstock and a reproach because of you. And why do you assert authority against us in the mountains?
verses.10:71: Now therefore, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us measure ourselves against one another there, for with me is the force of the cities.
verses.10:72: Ask and learn who I am and who the rest are who help us; and they say, 'You have no footing before us, because twice your fathers were routed in their own land.'
verses.10:73: And now you will not be able to withstand the cavalry and such a force in the plain, where there is neither stone nor pebble nor place to flee."
verses.10:74: Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, he was stirred in his mind, and he chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem, and his brother Simon met him to help him.
verses.10:75: And he encamped against Joppa, and those from the city shut him out, because a garrison of Apollonius was in Joppa; and they fought against it.
verses.10:76: And being afraid, those from the city opened up, and Jonathan became master of Joppa.
verses.10:77: And Apollonius heard of it, and he marshaled three thousand cavalry and a large force, and went toward Ashdod as though passing through, and at the same time he advanced into the plain, even because he had a multitude of cavalry and trusted in it.
verses.10:78: And he pursued after him to Ashdod, and the armies joined battle behind him.
verses.10:79: And Apollonius had left one thousand cavalry secretly behind them.
verses.10:80: And Jonathan knew that there was an ambush behind him. And they surrounded his army and shot the arrows into the people from morning until evening.
verses.10:81: But the people stood fast, just as Jonathan had commanded, and their horses grew weary.
verses.10:82: And Simon drew out his force and engaged the phalanx, for the cavalry was exhausted; and they were crushed by him and fled.
verses.10:83: And the cavalry was scattered in the plain, and they fled to Ashdod and entered Beth-dagon, their idol temple, to be saved.
verses.10:84: And Jonathan burned Ashdod and the cities around it, and took their spoils, and the temple of Dagon and its temple he burned with fire.
verses.10:85: And those who had fallen by the sword, together with those who were burned, amounted to eight thousand men.
verses.10:86: And Jonathan departed from there and encamped at Ashkelon, and those from the city came out to meet him with great honor.
verses.10:87: And Jonathan returned with those who were with him, having many spoils.
verses.10:88: And it happened, when King Alexander heard these words, that he honored Jonathan still more.
verses.10:89: And he sent him a golden buckle, as is the custom to be given to the Kinsmen of the Kings; and he gave him Ekron and all its borders as an inheritance.
verses.11:1: And the king of Egypt gathered numerous forces, like the sand along the shore of the sea, and many ships; and he sought to gain control of the kingdom of Alexander by deceit and to add it to his own kingdom.
verses.11:2: And he went out into Syria with peaceful words, and the people of the cities opened to him and met him, because it was the command of King Alexander to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.
verses.11:3: And as he entered the cities of Ptolemais, he stationed his forces as a garrison in each city.
verses.11:4: And as he approached Ashdod, they showed him the temple of Dagon burned down, and Ashdod and its surrounding towns torn down, and the bodies cast out, and those who had been burned, whom he had burned in the war; for they had made heaps of them along his way.
verses.11:5: And they recounted to the king what Jonathan had done, in order to find fault with him; and the king kept silent.
verses.11:6: And Jonathan met the king at Joppa with splendor, and they greeted one another and slept there.
verses.11:7: And Jonathan went with the king as far as the river called Eleutherus, and he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.11:8: Now King Ptolemy took control of the cities of the coast as far as Seleucia by the sea, and he was devising evil designs concerning Alexander.
verses.11:9: And he sent envoys to King Demetrius, saying, "Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander has, and you will reign over the kingdom of your father;
verses.11:10: for I regret having given him my daughter, for he sought to kill me."
verses.11:11: And he found fault with him because he desired his kingdom.
verses.11:12: And taking his daughter away from him, he gave her to Demetrius; and the face of Alexander was changed, and their enmity became evident.
verses.11:13: And Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the diadem of Asia; and he put two diadems around his head, that of Asia and Egypt.
verses.11:14: Now King Alexander was in Cilicia during those times, because the people of those places were revolting.
verses.11:15: And Alexander heard and came against him in war; and Ptolemy marched out and met him with a strong hand, and he routed him.
verses.11:16: And Alexander fled into Arabia to be sheltered there, and King Ptolemy was exalted.
verses.11:17: And Zabdiel the Arab cut off the head of Alexander and sent it to Ptolemy.
verses.11:18: And King Ptolemy died on the third day, and those who were in his strongholds were destroyed by those in the strongholds.
verses.11:19: And Demetrius became king in the one hundred sixty-seventh year.
verses.11:20: In those days Jonathan gathered those from Judea to attack the citadel in Jerusalem, and they made many siege engines against it.
verses.11:21: And some who hated their own nation, lawless men, went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was laying siege to the citadel.
verses.11:22: And on hearing, he became angry; and when he heard, he immediately broke camp and came to Ptolemais, and he wrote to Jonathan not to continue laying siege, and to meet him to confer at Ptolemais as quickly as possible.
verses.11:23: And when Jonathan heard, he gave orders to continue laying siege; and he selected some of the elders of Israel and of the priests, and he put himself in danger.
verses.11:24: And taking silver and gold and clothing and many other gifts, he went to the king at Ptolemais, and he found favor before him.
verses.11:25: And some lawless people from the nation were lodging complaints against him.
verses.11:26: And the king did for him just as those before him had done for him, and he exalted him before all his friends.
verses.11:27: And he confirmed the high priesthood to him, and whatever other honors he had previously, and he made him chief of the First Friends.
verses.11:28: And Jonathan requested the king to make Judea and the three districts and Samaria free from tribute, and they promised him three hundred talents.
verses.11:29: And the king consented, and he wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things to this effect:
verses.11:30: "King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan, greetings, and to the Jewish nation.
verses.11:31: We have also written to you the copy of the letter that we wrote to our kinsman Lasthenes concerning you, so that you may see it:
verses.11:32: 'King Demetrius to his father Lasthenes, greetings.
verses.11:33: We have decided to do good to the nation of the Jews, who are our friends and keep what is right toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.
verses.11:34: Therefore we have confirmed to them the territory of Judea and the three districts, Aphairema and Lydda and Rathamin (they were added to Judea from Samaria), and all things belonging to them, for all those who offer sacrifice in Jerusalem, in place of the royal dues which the king previously received from them each year from the produce of the land and the fruit of the trees.
verses.11:35: And the other things due to us from now on, from the tithes and the tolls due to us, and the salt pools, and the crowns due to us, we will grant all of them to them.
verses.11:36: And none of these things will be annulled from now on for all time.
verses.11:37: Now therefore take care to make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Jonathan, and let it be placed on the holy mountain in a suitable, conspicuous place.'"
verses.11:38: And King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and nothing opposed him, and he dismissed all his forces, each one to his own place, except the foreign forces which he had recruited from the islands of the nations; and all the forces from the time of the fathers became hostile to them.
verses.11:39: Now Trypho was previously one of those with Alexander, and he saw that all the forces were grumbling against Demetrius, and he went to Sinmalkue the Arab, who was raising Antiochus, the young boy of Alexander;
verses.11:40: and he pressed him persistently so that he would hand him over to him, so that he might reign in place of his father; and they reported to him all that Demetrius had done and the enmity with which his forces were hostile to him; and he remained there many days.
verses.11:41: And Jonathan sent word to King Demetrius to remove those from the citadel out of Jerusalem and those in the strongholds, for they were fighting against Israel.
verses.11:42: And Demetrius sent word to Jonathan, saying, "Not only will I do these things for you and your nation, but with honor I will honor you and your nation, if I find an opportunity.
verses.11:43: Now therefore you will do well to send us men who will fight alongside me, because all my forces have deserted."
verses.11:44: And Jonathan sent three thousand men, mighty in their strength, to Antioch, and they came to the king, and the king rejoiced at their arrival.
verses.11:45: And the people of the city gathered together into the middle of the city, about one hundred twenty thousand men, and they wanted to kill the king.
verses.11:46: And the king fled into the palace, and the people of the city seized the thoroughfares of the city and began to attack.
verses.11:47: And the king called the Jews for help, and they all gathered together to him at once; and they spread out in the city and killed in the city on that day about one hundred thousand.
verses.11:48: And they burned the city, and they took much plunder on that day, and they saved the king.
verses.11:49: And the people of the city saw that the Jews had gained control of the city as they wished, and they grew weak in their minds, and they cried out to the king with pleading, saying,
verses.11:50: "Give us the right hand, and let the Jews stop fighting against us and the city."
verses.11:51: And they threw down their weapons and made peace; and the Jews were honored before the king and in the sight of all those in his kingdom, and they returned to Jerusalem having much plunder.
verses.11:52: And King Demetrius sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him;
verses.11:53: and he proved false to all that he had said, and he became estranged from Jonathan, and he did not repay the acts of goodwill that he had rendered to him, and he afflicted him severely.
verses.11:54: Now after these things Trypho returned, and Antiochus with him, a very young boy; and he became king and put on a diadem.
verses.11:55: And all the forces whom Demetrius had dismissed in disgrace gathered together to him, and they fought against him, and he fled and was routed;
verses.11:56: and Trypho captured the elephants and gained control of Antioch.
verses.11:57: And Antiochus the younger wrote to Jonathan, saying, "I confirm the high priesthood to you, and I appoint you over the four districts and to be one of the friends of the king."
verses.11:58: And he sent him gold vessels and a table service, and he gave him authority to drink from gold vessels, and to wear purple, and to have a gold buckle.
verses.11:59: And he appointed his brother Simon governor from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.
verses.11:60: And Jonathan went out and traveled beyond the river and among the cities, and all the forces of Syria gathered to him as allies; and he came to Ashkelon, and the people of the city met him with honor.
verses.11:61: And he departed from there to Gaza, and the people of Gaza shut him out; and he laid siege around it, and burned its surrounding towns with fire, and plundered them.
verses.11:62: And the people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan, and he gave them the right hand; and he took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them away to Jerusalem, and he passed through the country as far as Damascus.
verses.11:63: And Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had arrived at Kedesh, which is in Galilee, with a large force, wanting to remove him from office.
verses.11:64: And he went to meet them, while he left his brother Simon in the country.
verses.11:65: And Simon encamped at Beth-zur, and he fought against it many days and shut it in.
verses.11:66: And they asked him that they might receive the right hand, and he gave it to them; and he expelled them from there, and seized the city, and placed a garrison over it.
verses.11:67: And Jonathan and his army encamped by the water of Gennesar, and they rose early in the morning and went to the plain of Nasor;
verses.11:68: and look, an army of foreigners was coming to meet him in the plain, and they had sent out an ambush against him in the mountains, while they themselves met him from the front.
verses.11:69: And those in ambush rose up from their places and joined battle; and all those with Jonathan fled;
verses.11:70: not even one of them was left behind, except Mattathias the son of Absalom and Judas the son of Chalphi, commanders of the army of the forces.
verses.11:71: And Jonathan tore his garments and put earth on his head, and he prayed.
verses.11:72: And he turned back to them in battle and routed them, and they fled.
verses.11:73: And those who had fled from him saw it and returned to him, and they pursued with him as far as Kedesh, as far as their camp, and they encamped there.
verses.11:74: And about three thousand men of the foreigners fell on that day; and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
verses.12:1: And Jonathan saw that the time was working in his favor, and he chose men and sent them to Rome to establish and renew the friendship with them.
verses.12:2: And to the Spartans and to other places he sent letters to the same effect.
verses.12:3: And they went to Rome, and they went into the council chamber and said, "Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews sent us to renew the friendship and the alliance for them as before."
verses.12:4: And they gave them letters to those in each place, so that they might escort them to the land of Judah in peace.
verses.12:5: And this is a copy of the letters that Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
verses.12:6: "Jonathan the high priest of the nation, and the council of elders, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, to the Spartans, their brothers, greetings.
verses.12:7: Already earlier, letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areus, who was reigning among you, stating that you are our brothers, as the copy below shows.
verses.12:8: And Onias welcomed with honor the man who had been sent, and received the letters in which it was clearly declared concerning alliance and friendship.
verses.12:9: Therefore, though we have no need of these things, having as encouragement the holy books that are in our hands,
verses.12:10: we undertook to send to renew the brotherhood and friendship with you, so that we might not become estranged from you; for many seasons have passed since you sent to us.
verses.12:11: We therefore at every time without ceasing, on the festivals and on the other appointed days, remember you at the sacrifices that we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.
verses.12:12: And we rejoice over your glory.
verses.12:13: Yet many afflictions and many wars surrounded us, and the kings around us made war against us.
verses.12:14: Therefore we did not wish to trouble you and the rest of our allies and friends in these wars.
verses.12:15: For we have the help from heaven helping us, and we were rescued from our enemies, and our enemies were brought low.
verses.12:16: Therefore we chose Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, and have sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
verses.12:17: Therefore we commanded them to go to you as well and greet you, and to deliver to you the letters from us concerning the renewal and our brotherhood.
verses.12:18: And now you will do well to answer us concerning these things."
verses.12:19: And this is the copy of the letters that they sent to Onias:
verses.12:20: "Ares, king of the Spartans, to Onias the great priest, greetings.
verses.12:21: It was found in a writing concerning both the Spartans and the Jews that they are brothers, and that they are of the lineage of Abraham.
verses.12:22: And now, since we have come to know these things, you will do well to write to us concerning your peace.
verses.12:23: And we also write back to you, 'Your livestock and your property are ours, and ours are yours.' Therefore we command them to report to you to the same effect."
verses.12:24: And Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had returned with a greater force than before to make war against him.
verses.12:25: And he departed from Jerusalem and met them in the country of Hamath, for he did not give them opportunity to invade his country.
verses.12:26: And he sent spies into his camp, and they returned and reported to him that thus they were positioning themselves to fall upon them during the night.
verses.12:27: And when the sun set, Jonathan ordered his men to keep watch and be at their weapons, to keep themselves ready for battle throughout the whole night; and he sent out sentries around the camp.
verses.12:28: And the adversaries heard that Jonathan and his men were ready for battle, and they feared and cowered in their hearts, and they kindled fires in their camp.
verses.12:29: But Jonathan and his men did not know until morning, for they saw the lights burning.
verses.12:30: And he pursued after them and did not overtake them, for they had crossed the Eleutherus River.
verses.12:31: And Jonathan turned aside against the Arabs called Zabadeans, and he struck them down and took their plunder.
verses.12:32: And breaking camp, he came to Damascus and marched through the whole country.
verses.12:33: And Simon went out and marched as far as Ashkelon and through the neighboring strongholds, and he turned aside to Joppa and seized it beforehand.
verses.12:34: For he had heard that they wanted to hand over the stronghold to Demetrius's men, and he stationed a garrison there so that they might guard it.
verses.12:35: And Jonathan returned and convened the elders of the people, and he took counsel with them to build strongholds in Judea,
verses.12:36: and to raise higher the walls of Jerusalem, and to raise a great height between the citadel and the city in order to separate it from the city, so that it would be by itself, so that they might neither buy nor sell.
verses.12:37: And they gathered together to build, and part of the wall of the brook on the east fell, and he repaired what was called Chaphenatha.
verses.12:38: And Simon built Adida in the Shephelah and fortified gates and bars.
verses.12:39: And Trypho sought to become king over Asia and to put on the diadem and to stretch out his hands against Antiochus the king.
verses.12:40: And he was apprehensive that Jonathan might not allow him and might make war against him, and he was seeking a way to seize him in order to kill him; and departing, he came to Beth-shan.
verses.12:41: And Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for battle array, and he came to Beth-shan.
verses.12:42: And Trypho saw that he had arrived with a great force, and he was apprehensive about stretching out his hands against him.
verses.12:43: And he welcomed him with honor, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and ordered his friends and his forces to obey him in the same way.
verses.12:44: And he said to Jonathan, "Why have you wearied all these people when no war is upon us?
verses.12:45: And now send them to their homes, and choose for yourself a few men who will be with you; and come with me to Ptolemais, and I will hand it over to you, and the rest of the strongholds, and the many forces, and all those in charge of affairs, and I will turn back and depart; for this is why I am here."
verses.12:46: And trusting him, he did just as he had said, and he sent away the forces, and they departed to the land of Judah.
verses.12:47: But he kept with himself three thousand men; about two thousand he left in Galilee, and one thousand went with him.
verses.12:48: And when Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him, and they killed with the sword all those who had come with him.
verses.12:49: And Trypho sent forces and cavalry into Galilee, to the Great Plain, to destroy all of Jonathan's men.
verses.12:50: And they learned that he had been seized and had perished, and those with him; and they encouraged one another and marched in close formation, ready for battle.
verses.12:51: And the pursuers saw that it was a matter of life for them, and they turned back.
verses.12:52: And they all came in peace to the land of Judah, and they mourned for Jonathan and those with him, and they were greatly afraid; and Israel mourned a great mourning.
verses.12:53: And all the nations around them sought to wipe them out, for they said, "They have no man leading and helping them; now therefore let us make war against them, and we will remove their remembrance from among mankind."
verses.13:1: And Simon heard that Trypho had gathered a large force to come into the land of Judah to destroy it.
verses.13:2: And he saw that the people were trembling and terrified, and he went up to Jerusalem and assembled the people.
verses.13:3: And he encouraged them and said to them, "You yourselves know all that I and my brothers and the house of my father have done for the laws and the sanctuary, and the wars and the distresses.
verses.13:4: For this reason all my brothers perished for the sake of Israel, and I alone was left.
verses.13:5: And now, far be it from me to spare my life in any time of affliction, for I am no better than my brothers.
verses.13:6: Rather, I will take vengeance for my nation and for the sanctuary and for our wives and children, because all the nations have gathered to destroy us out of hostility."
verses.13:7: And the spirit of his people revived upon hearing these words.
verses.13:8: And they answered with a loud voice, saying, "You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brother.
verses.13:9: Fight our battle, and everything that you say to us we will do."
verses.13:10: And he gathered all the fighting men, and hurried to finish the walls of Jerusalem, and fortified it all around.
verses.13:11: And he sent Jonathan the son of Absalom, and with him a considerable force, to Joppa; and he drove out those who were in it and remained there in it.
verses.13:12: And Trypho departed from Ptolemais with a large force to enter the land of Judah, and Jonathan was with him under guard.
verses.13:13: Now Simon encamped at Adida, facing the plain.
verses.13:14: And Trypho learned that Simon had risen in place of Jonathan his brother and that he was about to engage him in battle, and he sent envoys to him, saying,
verses.13:15: "Because of silver that Jonathan your brother owed to the royal treasury for the offices he held, we are detaining him.
verses.13:16: And now send one hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, so that when released he will not revolt against us, and we will release him."
verses.13:17: And Simon knew that they were speaking to him with deceit, yet he sent the silver and the boys so that he would not incur great hostility with the people,
verses.13:18: saying, "Because I did not send him the silver and the boys, he perished."
verses.13:19: And he sent the boys and the one hundred talents, but he lied and did not release Jonathan.
verses.13:20: And after these things Trypho came to invade the city and destroy it, and he circled around by the road to Adora. And Simon and his army marched opposite him to every place where he went.
verses.13:21: Meanwhile, those from the citadel kept sending envoys, urging him to come to him through the wilderness and to send them provisions.
verses.13:22: And Trypho prepared all his cavalry to come, but on that night there was very heavy snow, and he did not come because of the snow. And he departed and came into Gilead.
verses.13:23: And when he approached Baskama, he killed Jonathan, and he was buried there.
verses.13:24: And Trypho turned back and went away to his own land.
verses.13:25: And Simon sent and took the bones of Jonathan his brother, and buried him in Modein, the city of his fathers.
verses.13:26: And all Israel lamented him with a great lamentation, and mourned for him many days.
verses.13:27: And Simon built over the tomb of his father and his brothers, and raised it high to view with polished stone on the back and on the front.
verses.13:28: And he set up seven pyramids, one opposite another, for his father and his mother and four brothers.
verses.13:29: And for these he made elaborate structures, setting great pillars around them; and on the pillars he made suits of armor for an everlasting name, and beside the suits of armor, carved ships, to be seen by all who sail the sea.
verses.13:30: This tomb that he made is in Modein to this day.
verses.13:31: Now Trypho dealt deceitfully with Antiochus the young king and killed him,
verses.13:32: and became king in his place, and put on the diadem of Asia, and brought a great calamity upon the land.
verses.13:33: And Simon built the stronghold of Judea, and walled it around with high towers and great walls and towers and gates and bars, and placed food supplies in the strongholds.
verses.13:34: And Simon chose men and sent them to Demetrius the king to grant relief to the country, because all the deeds of Trypho were to plunder.
verses.13:35: And Demetrius the king sent to him according to these words, and answered him, and wrote to him a letter like this:
verses.13:36: "King Demetrius to Simon, high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and nation of the Jews: greetings.
verses.13:37: We have received the golden crown and the palm branch that you sent, and we are ready to make a great peace with you and to write to those in charge of affairs to grant you remissions.
verses.13:38: And whatever we established with you stands, and let the strongholds that you have built belong to you.
verses.13:39: And we remit to you oversights and offenses up to this day, and the crown that you owed; and if anything else was taxed in Jerusalem, let it no longer be taxed.
verses.13:40: And if any of you are qualified to be enrolled among those around us, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us."
verses.13:41: In the one hundred seventieth year the yoke of the nations was lifted from Israel.
verses.13:42: And the people of Israel began to write in the documents and contracts, "In the first year under Simon, great high priest and commander and leader of the Jews."
verses.13:43: In those days he encamped against Gaza and surrounded it with camps; and he made a siege tower and brought it up to the city, and struck one tower and captured it.
verses.13:44: And those in the siege tower leaped out into the city, and there was a great commotion in the city.
verses.13:45: And those in the city went up onto the wall with their wives and children, having torn their garments, and they cried out with a loud voice, begging Simon to give them the right hand.
verses.13:46: And they said, "Do not treat us according to our wicked deeds, but according to your mercy."
verses.13:47: And Simon came to terms with them and did not fight against them; but he drove them out of the city and cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and so he entered it singing hymns and giving blessing.
verses.13:48: And he cast out all uncleanness from it and settled in it men who practice the law; and he further fortified it and built for himself a residence in it.
verses.13:49: Now those from the citadel in Jerusalem were prevented from going out into the country and buying and selling; and they became very hungry, and a considerable number of them perished from famine.
verses.13:50: And they cried out to Simon to receive the right hand, and he gave it to them; and he drove them out from there and cleansed the citadel from the defilements.
verses.13:51: And he entered into it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches, and with lyres and cymbals and harps, and with hymns and songs, because a great enemy had been crushed out of Israel.
verses.13:52: And he established that this day be observed every year. And he further fortified the mountain of the temple that was beside the citadel, and he lived there, he and those with him.
verses.13:53: And Simon saw that John his son was a man, and he appointed him leader of all the forces; and he lived in Gazara.
verses.14:1: And in the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his forces and went into Media to obtain help for himself, so that he might fight against Trypho.
verses.14:2: And Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had come into his borders, and he sent one of his officers to capture him alive.
verses.14:3: And he went and struck the camp of Demetrius and captured him, and he brought him to Arsaces, and he put him under guard.
verses.14:4: And the land had rest all the days of Simon, and he sought good things for his nation; and his authority and his glory pleased them all the days.
verses.14:5: And along with all his glory, he took Joppa for a harbor and made an entrance to the islands of the sea.
verses.14:6: And he enlarged the borders for his nation and gained control of the country.
verses.14:7: And he gathered many captives, and he became master of Gazara and Beth-zur and the citadel; and he removed the impurities from it, and there was no one who opposed him.
verses.14:8: And they were tilling their land in peace, and the land yielded its produce, and the trees of the plains their fruit.
verses.14:9: Elders sat in the squares; all conversed about good things, and the young men put on glory and robes of war.
verses.14:10: For the cities he supplied food, and he equipped them with implements of fortification, until the name of his glory was named to the end of the earth.
verses.14:11: He made peace in the land, and Israel rejoiced with great gladness.
verses.14:12: And each one sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was no one making them afraid.
verses.14:13: And there ceased to be anyone fighting against them in the land, and their kings were crushed in those days.
verses.14:14: And he strengthened all the humble of his people; he sought out the law, and he removed every lawless and wicked person.
verses.14:15: He glorified the sanctuary, and he multiplied the vessels of the sanctuary.
verses.14:16: And it was heard in Rome that Jonathan had died, and as far as Sparta, and they were greatly grieved.
verses.14:17: But when they heard that Simon his brother had become high priest in his place and held control of the country and the cities in it,
verses.14:18: they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew with him friendship and the alliance which they had established with Judas and Jonathan his brothers.
verses.14:19: And they were read before the assembly in Jerusalem.
verses.14:20: And this is the copy of the letters which the Spartans sent: "The rulers of the Spartans and the city, to Simon the great priest and to the elders and to the priests and to the rest of the people of the Jews, brothers, greetings.
verses.14:21: The envoys who were sent to our people reported to us about your glory and honor, and we rejoiced at their arrival.
verses.14:22: And we recorded the things spoken by them in the resolutions of the people as follows: 'Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us, renewing the friendship with us.
verses.14:23: And it pleased the people to receive the men with honor and to place the copy of their words in the books designated for the people, so that the people of the Spartans might have a memorial; and they wrote a copy of these things to Simon the high priest.'"
verses.14:24: After these things Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a great golden shield weighing one thousand minas, in order to establish the alliance with them.
verses.14:25: Now when the people heard these words, they said, "What thanks shall we repay to Simon and to his sons?
verses.14:26: For he and his brothers and the house of his father stood firm, and they fought off the enemies of Israel from them." And they established freedom for it,
verses.14:27: and he inscribed it on bronze tablets, and they placed them on a pillar on Mount Zion. And this is the copy of the writing: "On the eighteenth of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, and this is the third year under Simon the high priest,
verses.14:28: in Saramel, in a great assembly of the priests and people and rulers of the nation and the elders of the country, it was made known to us:
verses.14:29: Since wars often occurred in the country, Simon the son of Mattathias, a son of the sons of Joarib, and his brothers gave themselves to danger and withstood the adversaries of their nation, so that their sanctuary and the law might stand, and they glorified their nation with great glory.
verses.14:30: And Jonathan assembled their nation and became high priest for them, and he was gathered to his people.
verses.14:31: And their enemies intended to invade their country in order to destroy their country and to stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.
verses.14:32: Then Simon arose and fought for his nation, and he spent much money of his own, and he armed the men of the army of his nation and gave them wages.
verses.14:33: And he fortified the cities of Judea, and Beth-zur, which is on the borders of Judea, where the weapons of the enemies were formerly, and he placed there a garrison of Jewish men.
verses.14:34: And he fortified Joppa, which is by the sea, and Gazara, which is on the borders of Ashdod, in which the enemies formerly lived, and he settled Jews there, and he placed in them whatever was necessary for their restoration.
verses.14:35: And the people saw the faithfulness of Simon and the glory which he purposed to bring about for his nation, and they appointed him their leader and high priest, because he had done all these things, and because of the righteousness and the faithfulness which he kept toward his nation; and he sought in every way to exalt his people.
verses.14:36: And in his days things prospered in his hands, so that the nations were removed from their country, and also those in the city of David, those in Jerusalem, who had made for themselves a citadel from which they went out and defiled all around the sanctuary and inflicted a great blow upon purity.
verses.14:37: And he settled Jewish men in it and fortified it for the security of the country and of the city, and he heightened the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.14:38: And King Demetrius confirmed the high priesthood to him in accordance with these things,
verses.14:39: and made him one of his friends, and glorified him with great glory.
verses.14:40: For it was heard that the Jews are called friends and allies and brothers by the Romans, and that they met the envoys of Simon with honor;
verses.14:41: and that the Jews and the priests were well pleased that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until a faithful prophet should arise,
verses.14:42: and that he should be commander over them, and that he should care for the sanctuary, that through him those over their works and over the country and over the weapons and over the strongholds should be appointed,
verses.14:43: and that he should care for the sanctuary, and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all contracts in the country should be written in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple and wear gold.
verses.14:44: And it is not lawful for anyone of the people or of the priests to nullify any of these things, or to contradict what will be spoken by him, or to convene a gathering in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or to wear a golden buckle.
verses.14:45: And whoever acts contrary to these things or nullifies any of these things will be liable."
verses.14:46: And all the people were well pleased to grant to Simon to act according to these words.
verses.14:47: And Simon accepted, and was well pleased to serve as high priest, and to be commander and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to preside over all.
verses.14:48: And they gave orders to place this writing on bronze tablets and to set them up in the precinct of the sanctuary in a secure place,
verses.14:49: and to place the copies of them in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons might have them.
verses.15:1: And Antiochus, son of King Demetrius, sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon, priest and ethnarch of the Jews, and to the whole nation.
verses.15:2: And their contents were in this manner: "King Antiochus to Simon, great priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.15:3: Since certain pestilent men have seized control of the kingdom of our fathers, I plan to lay claim to the kingdom so that I may restore it as it was before; and I have recruited a multitude of mercenary forces and prepared warships,
verses.15:4: and I intend to land in the country so that I may punish those who have destroyed our country and those who have laid waste many cities in the kingdom.
verses.15:5: Now therefore I confirm to you all the remissions that the kings before me granted you, and whatever other remissions they granted you;
verses.15:6: to strike your own coinage as currency for your country;
verses.15:7: and Jerusalem and the sanctuary are to be free; and all the weapons that you have prepared and the fortresses that you have built, which you hold, let them remain yours.
verses.15:8: And every royal debt and any future royal debts, from now and for all time, let them be remitted to you.
verses.15:9: And as soon as we establish our kingdom, we will glorify you and your nation and the temple with great glory, so that your glory will become manifest in all the earth."
verses.15:10: In the one hundred seventy-fourth year Antiochus went out into the land of his fathers, and all the forces came together to him, so that there were few with Trypho.
verses.15:11: And King Antiochus pursued him, and he came fleeing to Dor, which is by the sea.
verses.15:12: For he knew that troubles had gathered upon him, and the forces had abandoned him.
verses.15:13: And Antiochus encamped against Dor, and with him were one hundred twenty thousand fighting men and eight thousand cavalry.
verses.15:14: And he surrounded the city, and the ships closed in from the sea; and he pressed the city hard from the land and from the sea, and he did not allow anyone to go out or come in.
verses.15:15: And Numenius and those with him came from Rome with letters for the kings and the countries, in which these things were written:
verses.15:16: "Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.
verses.15:17: The envoys of the Jews have come to us as our friends and allies, renewing the original friendship and alliance, having been sent by Simon the high priest and the people of the Jews.
verses.15:18: And they brought a gold shield of five thousand minas.
verses.15:19: Therefore it has pleased us to write to the kings and the countries that they should not seek harm for them, nor make war against them or their cities or their countries, and that they should not ally themselves with those who make war against them.
verses.15:20: And it seemed good to us to accept the shield from them.
verses.15:21: If therefore any pestilent men have escaped from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest, so that he may punish them according to their law."
verses.15:22: And he wrote the same things to King Demetrius, and to Attalus, and to Arathes, and to Arsaces,
verses.15:23: and to all the countries, and to Sampsace, and to the Spartans, and to Delos, and to Myndus, and to Sicyon, and to Caris, and to Samos, and to Pamphylia and Lycia, and to Halicarnassus, and to Cos, and to Side, and to Aradus, and to Rhodes, and to Phaselis, and Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.
verses.15:24: And he wrote a copy of them to Simon the high priest.
verses.15:25: Now King Antiochus encamped against Dor a second time, continually bringing his troops against it and making siege engines; and he shut Trypho in from coming in or going out.
verses.15:26: And Simon sent him two thousand chosen men to fight as his allies, and silver and gold and abundant equipment.
verses.15:27: And he was unwilling to accept them, but annulled everything that he had agreed to with him before, and became estranged from him.
verses.15:28: And he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to confer with him, saying, "You hold control of Joppa and Gazara and the citadel in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
verses.15:29: You have laid waste their territories, and you have inflicted a great blow upon the land, and you have taken dominion over many places in my kingdom.
verses.15:30: Now therefore hand over the cities that you have captured, and the tributes of the places over which you have taken dominion, the territories outside Judea.
verses.15:31: And if not, give in place of them five hundred talents of silver, and for the destruction that you have caused and for the tributes of the cities, another five hundred talents; otherwise, they will come and wage war against you."
verses.15:32: And Athenobius, a friend of the king, came to Jerusalem, and he saw the glory of Simon, and a sideboard with gold vessels and silver vessels, and a large retinue; and he was amazed, and he reported to them the words of the king.
verses.15:33: And Simon answered and said to him, "We have neither taken foreign land nor held what belongs to others, but the inheritance of our fathers; yet it was wrongfully seized by our enemies at a certain time.
verses.15:34: But we, having the opportunity, hold fast to our inheritance and that of our fathers.
verses.15:35: And concerning Joppa and Gazara you make a demand; these were inflicting a great blow among the people and on our land; for these we will give one hundred talents." And he did not answer him a word.
verses.15:36: But he returned in fury to the king, and reported to him these words and the glory of Simon and all that he had seen; and the king became angry with great anger.
verses.15:37: Now Trypho boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.
verses.15:38: And the king appointed Cendebeus chief commander of the coastal region, and gave him infantry and cavalry forces.
verses.15:39: And he commanded him to encamp facing Judea; and he commanded him to build Kedron and to fortify the cities, and to make war against the people; meanwhile the king was pursuing Trypho.
verses.15:40: And Cendebeus arrived at Jamnia, and he began to provoke the people, and to invade Judea, and to take the people captive and kill them.
verses.15:41: And he built Kedron; and he stationed horsemen and forces there so that going out they might make raids along the roads of Judea, just as the king had ordered him.
verses.16:1: And John went up from Gazara and reported to Simon his father what Cendebeus was carrying out.
verses.16:2: And Simon called his two older sons, Judas and John, and said to them, "I and my brothers and the house of my father have fought the wars of Israel from youth until this day, and it has prospered in our hands to deliver Israel many times.
verses.16:3: But now I have grown old, and you, by mercy, are sufficient in years; take the place of me and my brother, and go out and fight in defense of our nation, and may the help from heaven be with you."
verses.16:4: And he chose from the country twenty thousand fighting men and horsemen, and they marched against Cendebeus and spent the night in Modein.
verses.16:5: And rising in the morning, they marched into the plain; and look, a large force was coming to meet them, infantry and horsemen, and a stream was between them.
verses.16:6: And he encamped facing them, he and his people; and he saw that the people were afraid to cross the stream, so he crossed over first; and the men saw him and crossed over after him.
verses.16:7: And he divided the people, with the horsemen in the middle of the infantry; and the cavalry of the adversaries was very numerous.
verses.16:8: And they sounded the trumpets, and Cendebeus and his army were routed, and many on his side fell wounded; and those who remained fled into the fortress.
verses.16:9: Then Judas, the brother of John, was wounded; but John pursued them until they came to Kedron, which he had built.
verses.16:10: And they fled into the towers that were in the countryside of Ashdod, and he burned it with fire; and about one thousand men of them fell, and he returned to Judea in peace.
verses.16:11: Now Ptolemy, the son of Abubus, had been appointed commander over the plain of Jericho, and he had much silver and gold,
verses.16:12: for he was the son-in-law of the high priest.
verses.16:13: And his heart was lifted up, and he desired to gain control of the country, and he plotted treacherously against Simon and against his sons to do away with them.
verses.16:14: Now Simon was inspecting the cities in the country and attending to their needs, and he went down to Jericho, he and Mattathias and Judas and his sons, in the one hundred seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month; this is the month of Shebat.
verses.16:15: And the son of Abubus deceitfully received them into the small fortress called Dok, which he had built, and he made a great banquet for them; and he hid men there.
verses.16:16: And when Simon and his sons were drunk, Ptolemy and those with him rose up, and took their weapons, and burst in upon Simon in the banquet hall, and killed him and his sons and some of his servants.
verses.16:17: And he committed great godlessness, and he repaid evil for good.
verses.16:18: And Ptolemy wrote these things and sent them to the king, so that he would send him forces for help and he would hand over their country and the cities.
verses.16:19: And he sent others to Gazara to do away with John; and to the commanders of thousands he sent letters to come to him, so that he might give them silver and gold and gifts.
verses.16:20: And he sent others to capture Jerusalem and the mountain of the temple.
verses.16:21: And someone ran ahead and reported to John at Gazara that his father and his brothers had perished, and said, "He has sent to kill you also."
verses.16:22: And when he heard this, he was deeply shocked, and he seized the men who had come to destroy him and killed them, for he knew that they were seeking to destroy him.
verses.16:23: Now the rest of the acts of John, and his wars, and the valiant exploits that he performed, and the building of the walls that he built, and his deeds,
verses.16:24: look, these are written in the book of the days of his high priesthood, from the time he became high priest after his father.

notes.1:1: Kittim (Greek Chettiim) refers here to Macedonia or the Greek world; the closing phrase "first over Greece" can mean either that Alexander had previously reigned over Greece or that he reigned as the first king of the Greek empire.
notes.1:4: The Greek text reads "dominions" (tyrannion, or "principalities"), whereas other manuscripts read "tyrants" or "rulers" (tyrannon).
notes.1:11: The Greek text uniquely combines the singular "a lawless son" with plural verbs ("they persuaded ... saying") and reads "separated by them" (hyp' auton), where other witnesses read plural "lawless sons" and "separated from them" (ap' auton).
notes.1:13: The Greek text uses the plural "they gave" (referring to the royal court), whereas other witnesses read singular "he gave"; a similar shift to plural verbs occurs in 1:24 ("they committed ... spoke").
notes.1:29: "Two full years" translates the literal Hebraic expression "two years of days" (dyo ete hemeron).
notes.1:48: The Greek text reads the verb "to profane" (bebelosai) rather than the noun "profanation" (bebelosei) found in other witnesses; similarly 1:47 reads "idols" (eidola) rather than "idol shrines" (eidolia).
notes.1:54: The Greek text reads "the forty-fifth year," omitting "one hundredth" found in other manuscripts that date the event to the one hundred and forty-fifth year of the Seleucid era (167 BC).
notes.1:55: The Greek text reads "windows" (thyridon) rather than "doors" (thyron) found in other witnesses.
notes.1:59: The Greek uses two distinct words for altar here, referring to the newly erected pagan altar (bomos) placed on top of the temple's sacrificial altar (thysiasterion).
notes.1:62: The Greek text reads "were hanged" (ekremasthesan), whereas other manuscripts read "stood firm" (ekrataiothesan).
notes.2:1: Joarim reflects the Greek spelling Ioareim, the Septuagint form of the priestly division Jehoiarib (1 Chronicles 24:7), where some Greek witnesses read Joarib.
notes.2:5: Sapphus translates the Greek reading Sapphous here (found in Codex Alexandrinus), whereas other Greek witnesses read Apphous (Apphus).
notes.2:8: The Greek text here reads endoxos ("an honored man"), as in Codex Alexandrinus, whereas other witnesses read adoxos ("a dishonored man" or "a man without honor").
notes.2:22: The Greek text here reads ton nomon ("the law") of the king, whereas other Greek manuscripts read ton logon ("the words") of the king.
notes.2:23: The Greek text here reads thymiasai ("to burn incense"), whereas other Greek manuscripts read thysiasai ("to sacrifice").
notes.2:26: Salom preserves the Septuagint form Salom (also in LXX Numbers 25:14), corresponding to Hebrew Salu.
notes.2:51: The Greek text here reads doxan aionion ("eternal glory"), as in Codex Alexandrinus, whereas other Greek manuscripts read onoma aionion ("an eternal name").
notes.2:54: The Greek text here reads hierosynes hagias ("a holy priesthood"), whereas other Greek manuscripts read hierosynes aionias ("an everlasting priesthood").
notes.2:58: The Greek text reads hos ("as it were, into heaven"), echoing Septuagint 2 Kings 2:11, whereas other witnesses read heos ("up into heaven").
notes.2:63: The Greek text here omits aurion ("tomorrow"), which appears in other witnesses ("and tomorrow he will not be found").
notes.2:66: The Greek text here has the second-person plural verb polemesete ("you will fight"), addressing Mattathias's sons together, whereas other manuscripts read the third-person singular polemesei ("he will fight"), referring to Judas.
notes.3:8: The Greek text reads 'upon it' (feminine singular, referring to the land of Judah); some manuscripts read 'out of it.'
notes.3:15: Greek 'and he proceeded, and ... went up' reflects a Hebraic idiom expressing continuation or addition (often understood as 'and moreover a strong army ... went up with him').
notes.3:16: The Greek text reads 'Methoron,' a textual variant of 'Beth-horon' (compare 3:24).
notes.3:25: The Greek text has two finite verbs ('began ... and terror fell'); some witnesses read an infinitive ('the fear ... and terror began to fall').
notes.3:30: Greek 'as once and twice' is a Hebraic idiom meaning 'as on former occasions.' The Greek sentence continues into verse 31.
notes.3:35: The Greek text reads 'to cast out' and singular 'its memory'; some manuscripts read 'to wipe out' and 'their memory.'
notes.3:41: The Greek text reads 'servants' (or 'slaves'), whereas some ancient versions read 'fetters.' 'Foreigners' translates Greek allophyloi, the standard Septuagint term used for the Philistines (contrast 'Philistines' for Phylistieim in 3:24).
notes.3:43: Some manuscripts add 'and let us fight for our people' before 'and of the sanctuary.'
notes.3:48: This clause is debated; the Greek literally indicates that they spread open the book of the law concerning the matters about which the nations consulted the likenesses of their idols.
notes.4:12: This Greek text reads echomenous ("close by / positioned"), whereas some manuscripts read erchomenous ("coming").
notes.4:15: This Greek text reads "Judea" (Ioudaias), whereas some manuscripts read "Idumea" (Idoumaias).
notes.4:23: This Greek text reads kai porphyran kai thalassian ("and purple and sea-purple"), whereas some manuscripts omit the second kai to read "sea-purple" (costly marine-dyed purple cloth).
notes.4:24: This Greek text has a single clause, "For His mercy is good forever" (Hoti kalon eis ton aiona to eleos autou), whereas some manuscripts repeat hoti ("For it is good, for His mercy is forever"), echoing Psalm 136:1 (135:1 LXX).
notes.4:30: Greek allophyloi ("foreigners," also in 4:12, 22, 26) is the standard Septuagint rendering for the Philistines, here recalling Jonathan's victory in 1 Samuel 14.
notes.4:33: This Greek text reads idontes ("those who have seen"), whereas other manuscripts read eidotes ("those who know").
notes.4:38: This Greek text includes "our" (hemon) with "sanctuary," whereas some manuscripts omit the pronoun.
notes.4:49: This Greek text reads "the altar of burnt offerings and incense" (ton holokautomaton kai thymiamaton), whereas other manuscripts read only "the altar of incense" (ton thymiamaton).
notes.4:61: The Greek phrasing literally reads "they fortified it to guard Beth-zur" (ochyrosan auto terein ten Bethsoura), which many interpreters understand in the sense of fortifying Beth-zur to guard it.
notes.5:3: The Greek text reads "in Judea" (en te Ioudaia), whereas other witnesses read "in Idumea" (Idoumaia).
notes.5:8: The Greek text reads "Jaze" (Iazen), where other witnesses read "Jazer" (Iazer); "its daughters" is a biblical idiom for dependent surrounding towns.
notes.5:15: The Greek shifts abruptly from third-person "against them" (ep' autous) to first-person "us" (hemas) within the messengers' report, where some witnesses smooth the first pronoun to "against us."
notes.5:16: The Greek text reads singular "by him" (hup' autou, apparently referring back to Timothy in v. 11 or to a collective enemy), while other witnesses read plural "by them" (hup' auton).
notes.5:22: The Greek text reads "the cities of Ptolemais" (ton poleon Ptolemaidos), whereas other witnesses read "the gate of Ptolemais" (tes pyles Ptolemaidos).
notes.5:26: The Greek forms "Alama" (Alamois) and "Makeb" (Makeb) correspond to "Alema" and "Maked" (Maked) in other witnesses; Bozrah (Bossora) and Bosor (Bossor) are two distinct Transjordanian towns.
notes.5:35: The Greek text reads "Maapha" (Maapha), whereas other witnesses read "Maspha" or "Malle."
notes.5:36: The Greek text reads "Chasphoth" (Chasphoth) and "Maked" (Maked), variant forms of "Casphor" and "Makeb" in v. 26.
notes.5:43: The Greek text reads "all his people in front of him" (emprosthen autou), whereas other witnesses read "behind him" (opisthen autou).
notes.5:50: The Greek text reads "the men of the city" (hoi andres tes poleos), whereas other witnesses read "the men of the force" (hoi andres tes dunameos).
notes.5:56: The Greek text reads "Zechariah" (Zacharias) for the second commander, whereas other witnesses (and vv. 18, 60) read "Azariah" (Azarias).
notes.5:67: The Greek text has singular pronouns ("while he wished ... when he went out"), whereas other witnesses read plural forms referring to the priests (compare also the singular "he" [auton] in v. 61, omitted in some witnesses).
notes.6:1: The Greek reads "in Elymais" (en Elymais), referring to the region in Persia; other manuscripts omit the preposition and identify Elymais itself as the city.
notes.6:2: Greek kalymmata chrysa literally means "golden coverings," often understood in this military context as golden shields or protective armor.
notes.6:20: This Greek text connects the date directly to the preceding verse; other manuscripts insert "and they gathered together and besieged them" before "in the one hundred fiftieth year."
notes.6:21: The Greek reads "from it, from the blockade" (ex autou ek tou synkleismou); other manuscripts read "some of them went out from the blockade."
notes.6:28: Greek tous epi ton henion ("those in charge of the reins") is a military idiom referring to cavalry or chariot commanders.
notes.6:37: The Greek reads "thirty-two men" per elephant (a well-known textual crux, sometimes thought to reflect a different underlying Hebrew term or number); "its Indian" refers to the elephant's Indian driver.
notes.6:43: This Greek text reads the surname "Sauaran" (other manuscripts read "Avaran") and "it appeared" (ophthe; other manuscripts read oiethe, "he supposed").
notes.6:49: This Greek text omits "peace" after "made/dealt" and reads singular "he went out," whereas other manuscripts read "made peace" and plural "they went out," referring to the garrison of Beth-zur.
notes.6:53: This Greek text reads "in the sanctuary" (en tois hagiois, matching 6:54); other manuscripts read "in the storage vessels" (en tois angeiois).
notes.6:61: This Greek text reads singular "he went out" (exelthen); other manuscripts read plural "they went out," referring to the defenders leaving the stronghold.
notes.7:1: The Greek text reads "the fifty-first year," omitting "and hundredth" found in other Greek witnesses (which date the event to year 151 of the Seleucid era, 162/161 BC).
notes.7:7: The Greek text reads the aorist indicative "he has punished" (ekolasato) rather than the imperative "let him punish" (kolasato) found in other witnesses.
notes.7:16: The active verb "he wrote" introduces the citation of Psalm 79:2-3 (LXX 78:2-3) in verse 17, referring to the psalmist or Scripture.
notes.7:25: The Greek text reads "that he was able to withstand them," lacking the negation "not" (ou) present in other Greek witnesses.
notes.7:31: The Greek text reads the place-name "Charpharsarama," whereas other Greek witnesses read "Capharsalama."
notes.8:5: Greek Kitieon ('Kittim,' originally inhabitants of Citium in Cyprus) is used in 1 Maccabees for the Macedonians, over whom Philip V and Perseus ruled.
notes.8:7: Greek diastole literally means 'separation, division, or specification' and is variously understood here as a stipulated settlement or a territorial partition ceded by Antiochus III (cf. v. 8).
notes.8:8: The Greek text names India and Media (alongside Lydia) rather than the Anatolian regions actually transferred to Eumenes II after the Peace of Apamea (188 BC), probably reflecting early confusion for Ionia and Mysia.
notes.8:10: The clause 'and plundered them' appears twice in the Greek text of this verse.
notes.8:26: The phrase 'to those waging war' is debated, referring either to enemies of Rome (who must not be supplied) or to allied forces fighting on Rome's behalf (without Roman provisions; compare 'those fighting as allies' in v. 28, where the Greek text omits 'ships').
notes.9:1: The Greek text here reads "had made war" (epoiēsen ... polemon), whereas other Greek witnesses read "had fallen in battle" (epesen ... en polemō).
notes.9:10: The Greek text lacks the conditional "if" (ei), reading "and our time has drawn near" rather than "and if our time has drawn near" as in other witnesses.
notes.9:13: The Greek text reads "by their camps" (apo tōn parembolōn autōn), whereas other witnesses read "from the sound of the camps" (apo tēs phōnēs tōn parembolōn).
notes.9:15: Greek Azōtou orous ("the mountain of Ashdod/Azotus"); because Ashdod lies on the coastal plain, scholars often suggest an underlying Hebrew phrase such as "the slopes of the mountain" or "Mount Hazor."
notes.9:33: The Greek text reads Asphal (compare Alasa in 9:5 and Iambrein/Iambrin in 9:36-37), where other Greek witnesses read Asphar (and Elasa, Iambri).
notes.9:42: The Greek text reads "the mountain of the Jordan" (to oros tou Iordanou), whereas other Greek witnesses read "the marsh of the Jordan" (to helos tou Iordanou; compare 9:45).
notes.9:50: Greek Thamnatha Pharathon appears as a single combined name without "and," and Tephon is widely identified with Tappuah. In 9:50-53 the Greek text uses plural verbs ("they returned," "they built," etc.), where other witnesses use singular verbs referring to Bacchides.
notes.9:52: The Greek text reads "the city, and Beth-zur" (tēn polin kai Bethsouran), distinguishing "the city" (Jerusalem) from Beth-zur, whereas other witnesses omit "and" and read "the city of Beth-zur."
notes.9:65: Greek ēlthen arithmō (literally "came with a number") reflects a Hebrew idiom (be-mispar) meaning "with a small number" of men.
notes.10:1: Greek ho Epiphanes ("Epiphanes") is nominative, modifying Alexander rather than Antiochus; Alexander Balas claimed descent from Antiochus IV and adopted his royal epithet.
notes.10:20: The clause "(and they sent him a purple robe and a golden crown)" is a third-person narrative parenthesis inserted directly within the quoted letter, with the plural verb apesteilan ("they sent") in the Greek text.
notes.10:29: "The price of salt" refers to the Seleucid salt tax, and "the crowns" refers to the customary gold crown levies paid to Hellenistic kings.
notes.10:42: The phrase "as in the former years" appears here in this Greek text (as in Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Venetus, echoing v. 41), separating "from the offices" from "of the sanctuary from the account."
notes.10:54: This Greek text reads singular pros auton ("with him"), where other witnesses read pros heautous ("with one another").
notes.10:64: This Greek text reads sindona ("fine linen," as in Codex Alexandrinus) rather than porphyran ("purple," as in other witnesses), and active ekeryxen ("he proclaimed") rather than passive ekerychthe ("it was proclaimed").
notes.10:84: This Greek text reads kai to hieron autes ("and its temple," as in Codex Alexandrinus), where other witnesses read kai tous symphygontas eis auto ("and those who had fled into it").
notes.11:3: The Greek text reads the genitive "of Ptolemais" rather than the nominative "Ptolemy" found in some witnesses as the subject of the verb.
notes.11:12: The Greek text reads "the face of Alexander was changed," a Semitic idiom for turning hostile; some witnesses instead read that Ptolemy became estranged from Alexander.
notes.11:18: The repeated phrase "in the strongholds" refers first to Ptolemy's garrison troops stationed in the fortified cities and second to the inhabitants of those same strongholds.
notes.11:28: The Greek text reads accusative "and Samaria" rather than genitive "of Samaria" and has the plural verb "they promised," referring to Jonathan together with the elders and priests.
notes.11:34: Aphairema and Rathamin are Greek Septuagint forms corresponding to Hebrew Ophrah (or Ephraim) and Ramathaim.
notes.11:38: The Greek text reads the plural pronoun "them" (referring to the foreign forces or Demetrius and his mercenaries), whereas some witnesses read singular "him" (Demetrius).
notes.11:39: Sinmalkue is the spelling in this Greek text (as in Codex Alexandrinus); other witnesses read Imalkue or Simalcue.
notes.11:50: Literally "right hands," the standard idiom for granting pledges of peace or terms of truce (also in 11:62, 66).
notes.11:56: The Greek word literally means "beasts" and is the standard Hellenistic military term for war elephants.
notes.11:67: Gennesar is the Greek form corresponding to Gennesaret, and Nasor is the Septuagint form corresponding to Hazor.
notes.12:20: The Greek text spells the Spartan king's name 'Ares' here (referring to Areus I, called 'Areus' in 12:7) and styles Onias 'great priest,' reflecting the Hebrew title for the high priest.
notes.12:26: The Greek text reads singular 'his camp' (referring to Demetrius's army), where some manuscripts read plural 'their camp.'
notes.12:28: The Greek text ends with the lighting of the campfires, leaving the enemy's nighttime withdrawal implicit until 12:29-30; other witnesses add 'and they departed.'
notes.12:37: 'The brook on the east' refers to the Kidron Valley east of Jerusalem; 'Chaphenatha' is an otherwise unattested name for a section of the wall or adjacent quarter.
notes.12:45: The Greek text reads 'the many forces,' where some other witnesses read 'the remaining forces.'
notes.13:18: The Greek text reads first-person apesteila ("I did not send"), reflecting Simon's perspective in anticipating the people's accusation, whereas other manuscripts read third-person apesteilen ("he did not send").
notes.13:21: The Greek text reads singular pros auton ("to him") rather than plural pros autous ("to them") found in other manuscripts, though the following clause uses plural "them."
notes.13:33: The Greek text begins with singular "stronghold" (to ochyroma) and repeats "towers" (pyrgois), whereas other manuscripts read plural "strongholds" throughout and omit the second "towers."
notes.13:43: The Greek text reads "Gaza" (Gazan), though the reference to "Gazara" in 13:53 (and elsewhere in 1 Maccabees and Josephus) indicates that the fortified city besieged here was Gazara (Gezer).
notes.13:45: "Give them the right hand" (Greek dexias didonai, literally "give right hands"; compare "receive the right hand" in 13:50) is an idiom for granting a pledge of safety or terms of peace.
notes.14:7: Gazara is the Hellenistic Greek name for the Old Testament city of Gezer.
notes.14:13: Some Greek manuscripts omit "their" and read simply "the kings," while the text translated here reads "their kings" (the kings of Israel's enemies).
notes.14:28: "Saramel" transliterates a debated Hebrew phrase variously explained as a place name, "court of the people of God" (the temple court), or a title of Simon, "prince of the people of God." The verb rendered "it was made known" is literally active ("he made known") in the Greek, used impersonally.
notes.14:43: The clause "and that he should care for the sanctuary" repeats the same clause from verse 42 in the Greek text, likely reflecting an early scribal duplication in the manuscript tradition.
notes.14:48: "In a secure place" is literally "in a faithful/reliable place," reflecting a Hebrew idiom for a firm or permanent place (cf. Isaiah 22:23).
notes.15:6: Our Greek text omits the verb clause "and I permit you" found in some other witnesses, leaving the infinitive "to strike" continuing the royal confirmation from verse 5 (where "remissions" also appears twice rather than "remissions ... gifts").
notes.15:18: Our Greek text reads "five thousand" minas here, whereas some other Greek manuscripts read "one thousand" minas (compare 14:24).
notes.15:23: Our Greek text preserves the distinct names "Sampsace" (Sampsake, often associated with Sampsame or Lampsacus) and "Caris" (Karida, where other witnesses read "Caria"), as well as "Arathes" in verse 22 (for Ariarathes V of Cappadocia).
notes.15:25: Greek en te deutera (literally "in the second") reflects a Hebraism for "a second time" (or possibly "on the second day"), and "troops" renders tas cheiras (literally "the hands," used for military detachments).
notes.15:31: Our Greek text reads the third-person plural "they will ... wage war" (ekpolemesousin), where other witnesses read the first-person plural "we will ... wage war."
notes.16:3: "By mercy" (en to eleei) and "from heaven" are reverent circumlocutions for God characteristic of 1 Maccabees.
notes.16:9: The unexpressed subject of "had built" is Cendebeus, who built Kedron in 15:41.
notes.16:10: Our Greek text reads "one thousand" men (where some other witnesses read "two thousand") and uses the feminine singular pronoun "it" referring to Ashdod (Greek Azotos).
notes.16:14: Our Greek text reads "and his sons" (kai hoi huioi autou), whereas some other manuscripts omit "and," identifying Mattathias and Judas as his sons.
notes.16:17: Our Greek text reads atheian ("godlessness" or "impiety"), whereas other Greek witnesses read athesian ("treachery").
